question: In adapting an ultrasound-guided dorsolateral quadratus lumborum block technique for rabbits, investigators initially targeted the level of the last thoracic vertebra but encountered difficulty maintaining a consistent needling plane and injection site. Which statements correctly explain the anatomic and procedural considerations that led to modifying the injection site? Select all correct options.
A: In rabbits, the last thoracic vertebra is T12 rather than T13, so direct transfer of a canine landmark can misplace the intended block level.
B: Caudal orientation of rabbit transverse processes can interfere with maintaining alignment between the ultrasound beam and needle plane.
C: Sliding the probe caudally to use an L1 injection site reduced acoustic shadowing from the T12 transverse process and required less probe pressure.
D: Applying firm probe pressure over T12 is preferred in live rabbits because it improves ventilation while stabilizing visualization of the quadratus lumborum fascia.
Contextual materials: To perform the QLB reported here, the ultrasound probe was positioned at the level of the last thoracic vertebra as previously described, which, in rabbits, is T12, as opposed to dogs, which is T13. Despite attempting to comply with current recommendations in the veterinary literature in terms of the level of the injection site for the QLB, these authors experienced difficulty in consistently achieving the same injection site in all subjects, and variability (between T12 and L1) was recorded in this study. The reason for this was potentially due to the anatomical variation between rabbits and dogs, with our dissections showing that rabbits’ transverse processes were oriented caudally, making it difficult to maintain the ultrasound needling plane with the ultrasound probe beam. In fact, in attempting to maintain the same injection site, the authors found it necessary to apply significant force with the probe against the T12 transverse process; however, the pressure required to maintain the probe in place while visualizing the targeted fascia would potentially compromise an alive patient’s ventilation. Therefore, the authors decided to perform this dorsolateral approach with middle-point injection into the QL fascia with the ultrasound probe slid more caudally using injection site L1 instead of between T12 and L1. This approach resulted in less acoustic shadowing from the T12 transverse process, and less pressure on the probe was required to visualize the relevant structures and the needle. Despite this adjustment, shadow interference from the T12 transverse process was still present in the ultrasound image in two out of ten rabbits. Despite species-specific ultrasound-guided loco-regional designed techniques, individual anatomic variability can still be present and further adjustments of the technique may be required.

question: In a comparative morphometric assessment of dairy cow ovaries, mean ovarian areas were evaluated separately for cows with mastitis and clinically healthy cows. The left ovary exceeded the right ovary by 6.97% in cows with mastitis, while in healthy cows the left ovary exceeded the right ovary by 10.51%, with this within-group difference statistically significant at p < 0.05. Between groups, the healthy cows' left ovary was 2.53% larger than the left ovary of cows with mastitis, and the right ovary of cows with mastitis was 1.3% larger than the right ovary of healthy cows; both between-group comparisons had p > 0.05. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: A statistically supported left-greater-than-right asymmetry was demonstrated within the healthy cow group.
B: In both health-status groups, the mean left ovarian area was numerically greater than the mean right ovarian area.
C: The data support a statistically significant reduction in left ovarian area associated with mastitis.
D: The right ovary was significantly larger in cows with mastitis than in healthy cows, indicating a mastitis-associated right ovarian enlargement.
Contextual materials: The mean areas of the left and right ovaries for both groups are presented in Figure 3. In the cows affected by mastitis, the left ovary was 6.97% larger than the right ovary. In healthy cows, the left ovary was 10.51% larger than the right ovary $( p < 0 . 0 5 )$ in the same group of cows. The left ovary in the healthy cows was 2.53% larger $( p > 0 . 0 5 )$ compared to that in the group of cows with mastitis in the left ovary. The right ovary in cows with mastitis was 1.3% larger $( p > 0 . 0 5 )$ than the right ovary in healthy cows.

question: In developing an in vitro maturation and parthenogenetic activation protocol for rat oocytes, which statements correctly describe the functional rationale for using cumulus-cell co-culture and activation stimuli? Select all correct options.
A: Cumulus cells can support oocyte redox homeostasis by converting cystine to cysteine, promoting cysteine availability, and increasing intra-oocyte glutathione.
B: Cumulus cells can metabolize glucose to pyruvate, which oocytes can use to support cytoplasmic maturation.
C: Chemical activators such as ethanol, ionomycin, and calcium ionophore primarily induce activation by suppressing intracellular Ca2+ release and maintaining meiotic arrest.
D: Effective parthenogenetic activation aims to reproduce fertilization-associated calcium signaling in metaphase-II-arrested oocytes, using physical or chemical stimuli that elevate intracellular Ca2+.
Contextual materials: Previous studies have shown the metabolic and protective role of cumulus cells, for example, cumulus cells can reduce cystine to cysteine, enhance the uptake of cysteine cumulus cells can reduce cystine to cysteine, and increase the intra-oocyte glutathione level and protect the oocytes against oxidative stress. Cumulus cells can also metabolize glucose to pyruvate that can be used by the oocyte to improve cytoplasmic maturation. There are many ways of parthenogenetic activation and can be induced both physically as well as chemically. The key is to mimic the physiology involved during the fertilization process i.e. Conveying Ca2+ signals to the metaphase-II arrested oocytes. For that purpose, many different modes of stimuli are being studied for example, Electric stimuli are long used to induce exogenous Ca2+ into the cytoplasm of mature oocytes. Also, many chemical activation agents have been studied as well like calcium ionophore, ethanol, and ionomycin they all increase intracellular Ca2+, which leads to activation of mammalian oocytes. Parthenogenetic activation opens a whole world of embryo development, either its SCNT, ISCI, or development of maternal genes only embryonic stem cells. It’s a field yet to be explored and exploited. Specifically, concerning rat parthenogenetic activation and embryo development is least understood as well as developed. Thus, based on previous studies we tried to develop an IVM co-culture protocol that may provide a key for the future development of transgenic rats in the in vitro environment and tried to access their developmental potential based on parthenogenetic activation, our studies can act as basic model to further study rat oocytes IVM and their developmental potential.

question: In a cat requiring smooth-pin stabilization involving the small sacrum, which technical or anatomic statements correctly describe safe and effective pin placement? Select all correct options.
A: Adequate stabilization requires two fixation points: one in the spinous process of the first or second sacral vertebra and one at the sacral roof.
B: A relatively shallow mediolateral angle is recommended when targeting the second sacral spinous process because it reduces the chance of contacting the dorsal branch of the second sacral nerve.
C: The preferred entry site in the sacral spinous process is at the transition between its middle and dorsal thirds, balancing anchoring strength against risk of vertebral canal penetration.
D: A 30–45 degree pin angle helps avoid the vertebral canal medially and the dorsal sacral foramina laterally.
Contextual materials: To achieve adequate stabilization of a smooth pin in the small feline sacrum, two fixation points are required: one at the spinous process of the first or second sacral vertebra and another at the sacral roof (Figure 1B). Ensuring a secure hold in the spinous process necessitates precise placement of the pin. Inserting the pin too dorsally in the spinous process may not provide suficient stability, while inserting it too ventrally risks penetrating the vertebral canal. Therefore, the optimal insertion point is at the transition from the middle to the dorsal third of the spinous process. This strategic placement minimizes the risk of vertebral canal penetration while maximizing the anchoring strength necessary for efective stabilization. The pin should be placed at an angle of 30–45 degree angle (Figure 1C) to avoid entering the vertebral canal medially and the dorsal sacral foramina laterally. Especially when targeting the second spinous process, a steep enough angle needs to be chosen to avoid the dorsal sacral foramen where the dorsal branch of the second sacral nerve emerges. The dorsal branches of the sacral nerves are interconnected and innervate the lateral and medial dorsal sacrococcygeal muscles, as well as the overlying skin areas. In the event of nerve irritation or injury, the likelihood of significant complications remains low due to the limited functional significance of the afected structures.

question: In a porcine cadaver study evaluating a fluoroscopy-guided celiac plexus injection technique, 2 mL of dye was injected to create a localized stained region for tissue collection and histologic assessment. Histology confirmed nervous fibers and/or ganglia compatible with the celiac plexus in submitted samples, but the entire plexus was not thoroughly dissected, and diffusion of local anesthetic, steroid, or neurolytic solutions was not tested. Which conclusions are methodologically justified? Select all correct options.
A: Use of 2 mL of dye establishes the optimal clinical injectate volume for porcine celiac plexus block because dye spread is equivalent to spread of local anesthetic and neurolytic solutions.
B: Confirmation of celiac plexus neural elements in sampled stained tissue supports that the injection reached plexus-associated structures, but it does not prove complete staining of the entire plexus.
C: If injectate diffusion fails to involve the entire celiac plexus, the resulting clinical block could be patchy and may provide incomplete visceral analgesia.
D: Extrapolating clinical efficacy from dye distribution alone is limited because long-acting local anesthetics with steroids for celiac plexus block and dehydrated ethyl alcohol for neurolysis may spread differently from dye.
Contextual materials: A thorough dissection of the CP was not performed, but it would have been desirable. It was not assessed if the plexus was entirely or only partially stained. We only confirmed the presence of nervous fibres and/or ganglia belonging to the CP in the submitted samples. The lack of complete diffusion through the whole CP might result in a “patchy” block and incomplete visceral analgesia. In this study, the most appropriate volume of injectate to be used for the technique was not established. It would be interesting to compare different aliquots to determine the most effective volume to block the CP under fluoroscopy guidance. We decided to use only 2 mL of dye to have a localized stained tissue, facilitating collection and histological evaluation. In clinical settings, larger volumes are used for CPB (increasing the chances of the block), even though the use of smaller volumes is advocated for neurolysis. As previously described, the spreading of the dye differs from the one of local anaesthetic or other (neurolytic) solutions. Specifically, longlasting local anaesthetics followed by steroids (e.g., triamcinolone) or dehydrated ethyl alcohol are usually employed in humans for the CPB and CPN, respectively. The specific spreading of these substances (strictly related with clinical effects) was not assessed in our model.

question: In adapting a biportal endoscopic lateral foraminotomy technique from human lumbosacral surgery to canine patients, which statements correctly explain why the approach and portal design require modification? Select all correct options.
A: The human vertebral isthmus docking strategy is poorly transferable to dogs because the vertebral isthmus is not well developed in the canine lumbar region.
B: The caudal border of the cranial articular process can serve as a more reliable canine docking point when human paraspinal docking landmarks are unsuitable.
C: Separate portal incisions of approximately 7 mm for the endoscopic portal and 10 mm for the working portal help accommodate instrument insertion and saline flow.
D: Canine lumbar transverse processes are shorter, broader, and more directly continuous with the dorsal arch than in humans, allowing direct use of the human technique.
Contextual materials: In human literature, a clear understanding of the relevant anatomical landmarks and procedural guidelines has been considered extremely important, and extensive research has been conducted on the topic. This emphasis arises from the fact that failure to follow these guidelines may result in complications such as prolonged surgical times, infections, postoperative hematomas, and dural tears. Our study aimed to clarify these principles by providing a detailed description of the BELF, based on current literature. However, direct application of human surgical methods to canine patients is impractical due to significant anatomical diferences. Notably, the canine iliac wing difers from that of humans; dogs possess a wider pelvis with more laterally oriented iliac crests, which afects musculature and overall biomechanics. In human lumbosacral surgery, the paraspinal skin approach typically utilizes the vertebral isthmus as a docking point. However, this structure is not well-developed in dogs. Additionally, canine lumbar TP projects more laterally, is significantly longer and narrower than in humans, and does not connect directly to the dorsal arch. Given these anatomical distinctions, we modified the surgical approach by designating the caudal border of the cranial AP as the docking point. This modification allowed for reliable anatomical reference points while maintaining procedural feasibility. To refine portal creation, we followed existing guidelines to determine appropriate incision lengths. Incisions were made at 7 mm for the endoscopic portal and at 10 mm for the working portal to ensure proper instrument insertion and smooth saline flow.

question: In a medium-sized dog undergoing maxillectomy, a surgeon plans preligation or clipping of arterial branches to reduce intraoperative hemorrhage. Reported approximate diameters in the region are: maxillary artery 4 mm, minor palatine artery 0.5 mm, major palatine artery 1 mm, sphenopalatine artery 2 mm, with the infraorbital and descending palatine arteries being similar in diameter. Which statements correctly interpret the expected vascular and clinical implications? Select all correct options.
A: Occluding both the infraorbital and descending palatine arteries would be expected to reduce blood flow to the maxilla more than occluding only one of these similarly sized branches.
B: Occlusion of the maxillary artery caudal to the origins of the infraorbital and descending palatine arteries would be expected to produce a greater reduction in maxillary blood flow than isolated occlusion of a small palatine branch.
C: Because the minor palatine artery is approximately half the diameter of the sphenopalatine artery, it would be expected to contribute more to hemorrhage control than clipping the sphenopalatine artery.
D: A large hemorrhage after osteotomy despite intended preligation would most plausibly indicate that hemoclips did not fully occlude the maxillary artery or relevant branches.
Contextual materials: Relative diameters of the maxillary artery and its branches in this area are reported to be approximately 4 mm (maxillary artery), 0.5 mm (minor palatine artery), 1 mm (major palatine artery), and 2 mm (sphenopalatine artery), respectively in a medium sized dog. The infraorbital and descending palatine arteries are reportedly of similar diameter. Given the similar diameter of the infraorbital and descending palatine arteries, diminution of blood flow to the maxilla would be greatest if both branches were occluded, or if the maxillary artery was occluded caudal to their origins. The location of hemoclip application was not recorded for the retrospective cases reported. Regardless, blood loss was found to be diminished compared to previous reports given that only three dogs with maxillary artery preligation developed intraoperative hypotension and one dog required an intraoperative blood transfusion (Figure 3). This would appear to be an improvement over the 30–50% of dogs requiring intraoperative transfusions as reported in the literature. In the one dog that required an intraoperative blood transfusion in the modified DL-IO group, a large degree of hemorrhage was reported following osteotomy with an oscillating bone saw. After discussing the case with the surgeon, they felt that the vascular clips may not have been fully across the maxillary artery or its branches, as additional clips were necessary at that location following tumor resection. Therefore, this hemorrhage was likely the result of inadequate hemoclip placement across the maxillary artery.

question: In feline perineal urethrostomy, caudal advancement of the pelvic urethra is needed to create a tension-free stoma while preserving function. Which statements correctly describe the anatomic and surgical considerations governing this urethral movement? Select all correct options.
A: The pelvic urethra primarily moves by caudal translation rather than by true elongation or stretching of the urethral wall.
B: Aggressive dorsal dissection is routinely preferred because the dorsal attachments are relatively devoid of clinically important nerves and blood vessels.
C: Adequate mobilization is generally achieved by blunt dissection of ventral and lateral tissues attaching to the pelvic urethra, helping reduce risks such as dehiscence and stricture.
D: The maximum safe caudal translation is constrained by the pelvic urethra's innervation and blood supply, including the length and location of nerves coursing dorsally.
Contextual materials: In this study, we characterized the movement of the pelvic urethra that occurs following PU, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously described. We have shown that the pelvic urethra translates, rather than stretches, and the challenge now is to develop strategies to increase the translation of the urethra to the maximum allowed by the innervation and blood supply of the pelvic urethra. When performing a PU, it is paramount to perform adequate mobilization of the urethra to avoid complications such as dehiscence and stricture. This is achieved by blunt dissection of the ventral and lateral tissues which attach to the pelvic urethra. The dorsal attachments include both the innervation and the blood supply to the pelvic urethra, and minimal blunt dissection is performed in this location. Aggressive dissection of the tissues dorsal to the pelvic urethra may increase the translation of the pelvic urethra but may also damage the innervation of the pelvic urethra, resulting in postoperative incontinence. It is possible that translation of the pelvic urethra will be increased by dissection of the tissues in this location. A detailed understanding of the location of the nerves and blood vessels dorsal to the pelvic urethra is required before dissection of the tissues in this location can be recommended. In addition, the length the nerves innervating the pelvic urethra will have to be determined as this is the factor which will determine the maximum extent to which the urethra can be translated caudally.

question: In comparative avian pulmonary anatomy, the ostrich lung has a rigid, flow-through ventilatory design with air capillaries surrounding pulmonary blood capillaries and epithelial plates at the air-capillary level. Which statements correctly describe the structural-functional implications of this arrangement? Select all correct options.
A: The avian flow-through ventilation pattern requires pulmonary capillaries to be unsupported during inspiration so that they can expand like mammalian alveoli.
B: Support from surrounding air capillaries helps permit a very thin but mechanically strong blood-gas barrier in a relatively non-compliant lung.
C: Homogeneous epithelial plates at the air-capillary level consist of two type I epithelial cells, whereas heterogeneous plates include both a type I and a type II cell.
D: Heterogeneous epithelial plates may contribute to surfactant production and serve as stem-cell reservoirs for the gas-exchange epithelium.
Contextual materials: The avian lung is generally noted to be non-compliant with a strong albeit very thin blood–gas barrier (BGB). These advantages for gas exchange have been attributed to the support of avian pulmonary capillaries by the surrounding air capillaries. This arrangement was made possible by the adoption of the flow-through system of ventilation in birds as opposed to the reciprocating pattern in mammals. In the ostrich lung, the epithelial plates were of two types due to the presence of two cell types at the air capillary level, namely, the homogeneous and the heterogeneous type. In the former case, the leaflets were made of two type I cells, while the heterogeneous type comprised a type I cell and a type II cell. The junctions of the bridges with the capillary walls show thickening of the epithelial cells and an accumulation of extracellular matrix. The support of the pulmonary capillaries may also be explained by an interdependence mechanism whereby the blood capillaries are linked to a rigid assemblage of air capillaries. Besides the support rendered to the blood capillaries in the ostrich lung, the heterogeneous type of plates participates in surfactant production and may act as reservoirs of stem cells for the gas exchange epithelium.

question: For procedures attempting needle access to the trigeminal cistern near the skull base in horses, comparative anatomy of the internal carotid artery (ICA) is clinically important. Which statements correctly describe the relevant anatomic and procedural risk considerations? Select all correct options.
A: In horses, the ICA passes from the roof of the medial compartment of the guttural pouch through the foramen lacerum and forms a sigmoid flexure just ventral to the trigeminal cave.
B: In humans, the ICA enters the cranial cavity through the carotid canal in the temporal bone rather than traveling through the foramen lacerum, although it subsequently courses superior to the foramen lacerum.
C: A trajectory that passes dorsally over the equine ICA and its sigmoid flexure would be expected to reduce the risk of arterial laceration compared with a ventral route that must cross the region of the flexure.
D: A ventral approach to the equine trigeminal cistern minimizes carotid risk because the needle trajectory remains caudal and superficial to the sigmoid flexure throughout its course.
Contextual materials: In humans, perforation of the ICA with the injecting needle can result in serious complications, including pseudoaneurysm formation, caroticocavernous fistula, ICA rupture, and potentially life-threatening arterial hemorrhage. Unlike in horses, the ICA of humans does not travel through the foramen lacerum but instead passes through the carotid canal within the temporal bone to enter the cranial cavity. It then courses superior to the foramen lacerum, a segment referred to as the lacerum segment. Inadvertent puncture of the ICA during percutaneous cannulation of the foramen ovale can occur at several anatomical locations: its extracranial portion at its entrance in the carotid canal, at the exocranial surface of the skull base in the foramen lacerum or at its intracranial portion, such as within the cavernous sinus. The minimal distances from the foramen ovale to the trigeminal ganglion and the intracranial portion of the ICA have been measured, and guidelines for safe advancement of the needle have been established. In contrast, in horses, the ICA travels from the roof of the medial compartment of the guttural pouch through the foramen lacerum, perforating its cartilage plate through a slit-shaped opening located beneath its rostrolateral edge, and subsequently forms the sigmoid flexure - a segment located just ventral to the trigeminal cave. The only possible ventral and/or lateral access route to the trigeminal cistern is through the foramen lacerum. This inherently carries a high risk of lacerating the sigmoid flexure, which is further amplified with the ventral approach, where the needle must cross the center of the sigmoid flexure. Thus, even an accuracy aberration of only a few millimeters over a total trajectory length of approximately 20 cm would result in its perforation. In seven out of eight cadaveric specimens that underwent the VNA, hemorrhage was observed at the needle insertion site in the roof of the guttural pouch - most likely originating from the carotid artery or the sinus petrosus. The results of the present study suggest that this complication could be avoided by electing the TLNA, as this would result in a trajectory dorsally “flying over” the ICA and its sigmoid flexure to reach the trigeminal cistern (Figure 3).

question: A controlled 16-week trial in 44-week-old Lohmann Brown laying hens evaluates a 0.5% drinking-water probiotic containing Lactobacillus acidophilus KUEN 1607 and Pediococcus acidilactici KUEN 1608. Which findings would be consistent with a beneficial probiotic effect on production, intestinal function, systemic physiology, and skeletal assessment in this type of study? Select all correct options.
A: Improved feed conversion ratio accompanied by greater eggshell strength and thickness, improved albumen quality, and fewer cracked or shell-less eggs.
B: Lower yolk and serum cholesterol concentrations together with improved antioxidant indices and increased serum IgG.
C: A reduced jejunal villus-height-to-crypt-depth ratio associated with decreased fecal Lactobacillus spp. and increased coliform counts.
D: No significant change in bone volume or surface area by conventional measures, but subtle long-bone shape differences detected by 3D geometric morphometric analysis, especially in the femur and tibiotarsus.
Contextual materials: This study investigated the effects of probiotic supplementation on performance, egg quality, antioxidant capacity, gut morphology, fecal microbiota, and bone morphology in Lohmann Brown laying hens aged 44 weeks over a 16-week period. Ninety-six hens were randomly divided into control and probiotic groups $( \mathrm { n = 4 8 \ e a c h } )$ . The probiotic group received probiotic supplement containing Lactobacillus acidophilus KUEN 1607 and Pediococcus acidilactici KUEN 1608 via drinking water at 0.5%. Probiotic supplementation significantly improved feed conversion ratio (FCR), eggshell strength and thickness, and albumen quality $( p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ and reduced the incidence of cracked and shell-less eggs $( p < 0 . 0 5 )$ . Yolk and serum cholesterol levels decreased $( p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , and antioxidant parameters improved, along with elevated serum IgG $( p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ . Histological analysis showed an increased ratio of villus height to crypt depth $( p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ in the jejunum, indicating enhanced intestinal health. Fecal samples revealed increased Lactobacillus spp. and reduced coliform counts $( p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , suggesting improved gut microbiota balance. While bone volume and surface area showed no significant difference, 3D geometric morphometric analysis identified subtle shape changes in long bones, especially the femur and tibiotarsus. question: In a poultry nutrition trial comparing pelleted and mash diets in two hen breeds, investigators assess small-intestinal villus height (VH), crypt depth (CD), and villus height-to-crypt depth ratio (VCR). Pelleted diets are associated with increased VH and CD in the small intestine and increased VCR in the duodenum, and a feed-form-by-breed interaction is detected for VH in the duodenum and ileum. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: Greater villus height is consistent with increased mucosal surface area for nutrient absorption.
B: An increased duodenal VCR is generally interpreted as reduced nutrient digestibility and poorer growth potential.
C: A significant feed-form-by-breed interaction for VH indicates that the morphological response to pellets versus mash may differ among breeds.
D: The larger VH and CD with pelleted feed are most plausibly explained by lower feed intake and reduced nutrient flow through the proximal small intestine.
Contextual materials: The small intestine is the main organ in the gastrointestinal tract, its structure supports the digestion and absorption of nutrients such as VH, CD and VCR, which can reflect the functional status of small intestine. The longer VH might be combined with increased surface area and hence greater absorption. Higher VCR indicated higher intestinal secretory ability and may lead to greater nutrient digestibility and growth performance of chickens. In the current study, a greater VH and CD in the small intestine, as well as a higher VCR in the duodenum, were observed in both breeds of hens fed with pellets than mash. This histomorphological finding aligns with the results of Abadi et al. that show birds fed with pelleted diets had a greater value of VH and VCR in the duodenum and jejunum in male Ross 308 chickens than those fed with mash diets. Dahlke et al. also reported that reduction in the particle size of the diets led to shallower crypts and shorter duodenal villi. Higher VH and CD in the small intestine of birds fed pellet was thought to be caused by the higher feed intake and higher flow of nutrients in the proximal small intestine. Interactions between feed form and breed for the VH of duodenum and ileum indicated that changes in the morphological structures could be breed-specific when feeding different feed forms.

question: In a comparative assessment of cattle breeds, body weight was positively associated with claw base area within individuals, but high-productive breeds had relatively smaller claw bases than Highland cattle. Which statements correctly interpret the biomechanical and breeding implications of these findings? Select all correct options.
A: A heavier cow would generally be expected to have a larger absolute claw base area, but this does not necessarily mean that pressure per square centimeter is the same across breeds.
B: The observation that body weight and claw base area are related within individuals proves that breed has no independent effect on claw morphology.
C: If high-productive breeds have smaller claw bases relative to body mass, their static load per unit claw-base area would be higher than that of a breed with relatively larger claws.
D: Selection for increased body weight without directly selecting for larger claws could plausibly increase claw loading and affect both animal locomotor health and pasture impact.
Contextual materials: Body weight and claw base were closely related at the individual level: The heavier a cow was, the larger was the area of its claw base. However, breed did also matter: Relatively small claws were measured for the two high-productive breeds compared to those of Highland cattle. Therefore, the static pressure of body mass on every square centimeter of claw base was relatively high for Angus × Holstein, marginally less for Original Braunvieh, and significantly lower for Highland cattle. The similar weightclaw allometry of the two productive breeds goes along with Tuohy et al., who found only small diferences in weightclaw allometry between Holstein and Holstein × Jersey dairy cows. The relatively large claws of Highland cattle have been presumed, but have never been quantified in a comparative assessment. For this experiment, cows where kept under similar, but not identical housing condition over winter. To increase comparability, they grazed the same grounds over a period of 10 weeks prior to the claw measurement. An explanation for the diferences observed among breeds may be that the breeding process increased cattle’s body weights to a much larger extent than their claw bases—likely because nobody declared “large claws” as a breeding objective. These diferences may strongly afect the animals as well as the pastures they graze.

question: In a morphometric study of the equine eye and orbit, Spearman correlation coefficients were used to evaluate associations among orbital cavity dimensions, eyeball dimensions, lens dimensions, and anterior/posterior chamber widths, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Which statements accurately reflect the reported correlation pattern? Select all correct options.
A: Lens length was significantly correlated with multiple eyeball and orbital cavity measurements, making it a stronger general predictor of globe and orbital size than lens width.
B: Orbital cavity height was significantly correlated with orbital cavity length and with all measured eyeball dimensions, whereas orbital cavity length was significantly correlated with eyeball length but not with every eyeball dimension.
C: Lens height and lens width showed a strong significant correlation, lens height and lens length showed only a weak significant correlation, and lens width and lens length were not significantly correlated.
D: Anterior and posterior chamber widths were moderately correlated with each other, but posterior chamber width was not significantly correlated with eyeball length and anterior chamber width was not significantly correlated with lens length.
Contextual materials: $p = 0 . 0 1 5 )$ . A strong correlation was found between width and height $( \rho = 0 . 7 0 4 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ Orbital cavity height and length were significantly correlated $( \rho = 0 . 6 3 9 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , indicating a strong association. Orbital cavity height also showed significant correlations with all eyeball measurements: width $( \rho = 0 . 3 6 0 ; p = 0 . 0 1 9 )$ , height $( \rho = 0 . 4 1 9 ; p = 0 . 0 0 6 )$ and length $( \rho = 0 . 5 4 2 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ . In contrast, orbital cavity length was only correlated with eyeball length $( \rho = 0 . 4 2 2 ; p = 0 . 0 0 5 )$ . Lens dimensions showed varying degrees of correlation. A strong correlation was found between lens height and lens width $\left( \rho = 0 . 7 8 8 ; \right.$ $p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , while a weak correlation was observed between lens height and lens length $( \rho = 0 . 3 0 6 ; p = 0 . 0 4 8 )$ . No significant correlation was found between lens width and lens length $( \rho = 0 . 2 7 9 ; p = 0 . 0 7 4 )$ . Lens width demonstrated moderate-to-weak correlations with several eyeball and orbital cavity measurements: eyeball width $( \rho = 0 . 3 4 6 ; p = 0 . 0 2 5 )$ eyeball height $( \rho = 0 . 3 3 2 ; p = 0 . 0 3 2 )$ , eyeball length $( \rho = 0 . 5 2 3 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , orbital cavity height $( \rho = 0 . 3 4 9 ; p = 0 . 0 2 3 )$ , and orbital cavity length $( \rho = 0 . 4 8 4 ; p = 0 . 0 0 1 )$ . Lens height showed moderate correlations with eyeball length $( \rho = 0 . 5 3 8 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , orbital cavity height $( \rho = 0 . 4 3 5 ; p = 0 . 0 0 4 )$ , and orbital cavity length $( \rho = 0 . 5 3 9 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ . Conversely, lens length was not significantly correlated with any eyeball or orbital cavity measurements. Finally, the widths of the posterior and anterior chambers were moderately correlated $( \rho = 0 . 5 8 0 ; p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ ). Both variables showed weak to moderate correlations with all eyeball, orbital cavity, and lens dimensions $( \rho = 0 . 3 3 7 - 0 . 6 5 0 ; p = 0 . 0 2 9 \mathrm { ~ t o ~ } < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ , except for the posterior chamber width with eyeball length $( \rho = 0 . 2 3 2 ; p = 0 . 1 4 0 )$ , and the anterior chamber width with lens length $( \rho = 0 . 2 0 4 ; p = 0 . 1 9 5 )$ , which were not statistically significant.

question: In ultrasonographic estimation of thyroid volume in goats, maximum length, width, and height may be multiplied by a geometric correction factor. Which statements correctly interpret the use of correction factors when caprine thyroid shape differs from an ideal ellipsoid? Select all correct options.
A: The conventional ellipsoid correction factor of π/6, approximately 0.524, may underestimate volume when most thyroid glands are not ellipsoid or oval in shape.
B: A modified correction factor of π/4, approximately 0.785, can bring ultrasonographic thyroid volume estimates closer to grossly measured caprine thyroid volumes in a population with mostly non-oval glands.
C: If only a small minority of caprine thyroids are oval-shaped, shape mismatch is a plausible explanation for poor precision of the general ellipsoid formula.
D: Because Brunn's 0.479 factor is smaller than π/6, it would be expected to increase calculated thyroid volume relative to the conventional ellipsoid formula when the same linear dimensions are used.
Contextual materials: For calculation of the thyroid volume based on the maximum length, width and height, the ellipsoid formula $( \mathbb { E } \mathbb { q } 1 )$ is commonly used. The correction factor in that equation is p (= 0.524). In 1981, Brunn et al. proposed a modified correction factor of 0.479, as more precise compared to the previous one. In 2006, Shabana et al. compared the results of the US volume measured using different correction factors with the results of the volume obtained in the computed tomography and proposed another factor of 0.529, as an average of the acceptable range 0.494–0.554. In the current study, the correction factor $\mathrm { o f } { \frac { \pi } { 6 } }$ was initially used, as widely accepted in human and veterinary medicine. However, due to the discrepancy between the results of US and gross volume, a modified correction factor of $\textstyle { \frac { \pi } { 4 } } ( = 0 . 7 8 5 )$ was introduced. The volume calculated this way $\left( \operatorname { E q } 2 \right)$ was $1 . 6 2 \pm 0 . 6 1 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 } .$ , which is similar to the grossly measured $1 . 6 4 \pm 0 . 6 9 \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 }$ . For comparison, the mean volume calculated using the general formula (Eq 1) was $1 . 0 6 \pm 0 . 4 0 ~ \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 } .$ . The cause of this disparity was presumably the fact that only 9% of caprine thyroids were oval-shaped, i.e. similar to an ellipsoid, thus fitted well to the general ellipsoid formula. For other thyroid shapes this formula turned out to be much less precise.

question: When planning a femoral nerve block in pigs using the iliopsoas compartment as the target region, which anatomical and procedural statements are correct? Select all correct options.
A: The ventral branches of lumbar spinal nerves join within the iliopsoas compartment to form the lumbar plexus, from which the femoral nerve receives contributions.
B: Because the femoral nerve may arise from multiple lumbar segments over a relatively broad area, depositing injectate too far cranially may produce an incomplete block if the nerve is targeted before the contributing branches have united.
C: A contribution from L4, when present, is typically a large branch that is easier to identify in fetal specimens than in mature pigs.
D: Variation in the lumbar roots contributing to the femoral nerve cannot be attributed simply to having a different number of lumbar vertebrae, because most pigs in the compared observations had six lumbar vertebrae despite differing root patterns.
Contextual materials: The preceding anatomical study was useful to establish an adequate acoustic window for subsequent injections. The anatomical features of the FN in the iliopsoas compartment, and adjacent structures in the lumbosacral region were similar to previous descriptions in small mammals. The ventral branches of the lumbar spinal nerves joined together in the iliopsoas compartment forming the lumbar plexus. In the pigs used for anatomical dissection, we found that branches of L4–L6 supplied the FN. This result deviates slightly from the information in literature. According to a standard anatomical textbook, only L5 and L6 supply the FN in pigs. Herrera et al. reported that L5 and L6 supply the FN in only 26.7% of investigated pig foetuses, whereas 66.7% showed L4 and L5, and 6.6% L3 and L4 to supply the FN. We found that the branch provided by L4 was a really delicate nerve. It can be difficult to find such thin nerves in foetuses. Segmental involvement may also be related to the breed or number of lumbar vertebrae. The latter assumption is not supported by the fact that, like in all our pigs, 96.7% (n = 29) of those in the study of Herrera et al. had six lumbar vertebrae. The number of lumbar segments involved in the FN, and thus the width of its area of origin, could result in insufficient blockade if the injection, for example, is too far cranial. This shows the importance of reaching the FN as targeted as possible and after union of involved lumbar nerves.

question: A cat with a mid-antebrachial diaphyseal fracture involving the radius and ulna is being considered for minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis (MIPO) of the radius. Which statements correctly describe reduction and stabilization principles for this type of injury? Select all correct options.
A: For diaphyseal fractures treated with MIPO, the primary goal is functional reduction rather than exact anatomical reconstruction of every fragment, with restoration of bone length and alignment in frontal, sagittal, and axial planes.
B: In cats with mid-antebrachial radius-ulna fractures, stabilizing only the radius is generally preferred because ulnar fixation increases the risk of non-union.
C: Cadaveric fracture reductions may appear easier than clinical reductions because they lack post-traumatic swelling, hematoma, and skeletal muscle contracture.
D: When severe skeletal muscle contracture prevents simple traction reduction, adjunctive methods such as a hanging-limb technique, skeletal traction table, external fixation, or intramedullary pinning may be needed before final reduction under the plate.
Contextual materials: The absence of post-traumatic changes associated with the fracture, such as swelling, hematoma, and skeletal muscle contracture, may also be considered a limitation, as reduction in fractures in cadavers without these changes was easier. Treatment of diaphyseal fractures with MIPO does not require anatomical reduction of bone fragments. The aim is functional reduction. It is important to restore bone length and alignment in the frontal, sagittal, and axial planes. In our study, initial reduction in fractures required only manual traction of the antebrachium and manipulation of the paw. Final reduction was performed after insertion and fixation of a pre-contoured plate. In clinical cases, especially in patients with severe skeletal muscle contractures, more forceful reduction methods should be used prior to final reduction of the fracture under the plate, such as the hanging-limb technique, intramedullary pinning, skeletal traction table, or external fixator. For radial and ulnar fractures, it is possible to reduce the fractures indirectly after intramedullary pinning of the ulna. In this study, ulnae were not reduced or stabilized in order to test the usefulness of a contoured radial plate as a reduction tool; however, ulna fractures in cats should be stabilized. In most cases, the ulnar plates may be a better choice than intramedullary pins. Stabilization of the radius only in cats with mid-antebrachial fractures using type II external skeletal fixators has been reported as a risk factor for the development of non-union.

question: A radiographic survey of clinically sound warmblood sport horses identifies a congenital caudal cervical morphologic variant involving C6 in approximately 30% of horses. In related case-control work, similar C6 variants have been reported more frequently in unaffected controls than in clinically affected horses. The survey finds no negative association with clinical soundness or competition performance, but it does not include direct biomechanical testing. Which interpretations are justified? Select all correct options.
A: Detection of the C6 variant alone is sufficient evidence that the horse’s cervical pain or poor performance is caused by the variant.
B: The finding is more consistent with an anatomical variation than with an inherently performance-limiting malformation.
C: A proposed protective effect through altered force distribution in the caudal cervical spine remains speculative without biomechanical assessment.
D: A prevalence near 30% supports the view that warmblood populations may be relatively commonly affected by this variant.
Contextual materials: The high prevalence of ECCMV in the investigated, clinically sound sport horse population and the results of two recent studies where congenital variants of C6 occurred more frequently in controls compared with cases, support the hypothesis formulated by Veraa et al. that these morphologic changes might even indicate a beneficial adaption in warmbloods. Alterations in the morphology of C6 could influence the distribution of biomechanical forces within the caudal cervical spine, potentially reducing mechanical stress on adjacent structures such as the APJ. However, the present study was not designed to assess biomechanical function; therefore, any presumed beneficial effect remains speculative. Nonetheless, the absence of negative associations with clinical soundness or competition performances in the present research further supports the interpretation of ECCMV as an anatomical variation rather than a performance-limiting malformation. Moreover, this study determined a prevalence of 30% which reinforces the assumption that warmblood breeds are more frequently affected.

question: In a sheep lung-tumor investigation involving suspected ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA), lesions are evaluated grossly, histologically, immunohistochemically, and by viral assays. Which statements correctly describe patterns expected for OPA and associated myxoid growths? Select all correct options.
A: The diaphragmatic lung lobes may be most commonly affected, with classical OPA predominating over atypical OPA; atypical cases can include solitary myxomatous nodules.
B: Ki67 proliferative labeling is expected to be higher in atypical OPA and myxoid growths than in classical OPA.
C: Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus matrix antigen is expected to be restricted to epithelial neoplastic cells and absent from mesenchymal cells, with exogenous virus typically undetectable by PCR.
D: Neoplastic pulmonary adenocarcinoma cells can immunolabel for broad-spectrum cytokeratin and TTF-1, whereas associated myxoid growths can immunolabel for Vimentin, Desmin, and smooth muscle actin.
Contextual materials: Results: Out of 2693 examined sheep, 34 had OPA (1.26% prevalence). The diaphragmatic lobes were the most affected. Grossly, the classical OPA was identified in 88.24% of investigated cases and the atypical OPA in 11.76% that included solitary myxomatous nodules. Histopathology results confirmed the presence of OPA in all suspected cases, which were classified into acinar and papillary types. Myxoid growths (MGs) were diagnosed in 6 classical OPA cases and in 2 cases of atypical form. Lung adenocarcinoma was positive for MCK and TTF-1, and MGs showed immunoreaction for Vimentin, Desmin and SMA; Ki67 expression of classical OPA was higher than atypical OPA and MGs. JSRV-MA was identified by IHC (94.11%) in both epithelial and mesenchymal cells of OPA. Immunocytochemistry and electron microscopy also confirmed the JSRV within the neoplastic cells. ExJSRV was identified by PCR in 97.05% of analyzed samples. Phylogenetic analysis revealed the presence of the exJSRV type 2 (MT809678.1) in Romanian sheep affected by lung cancer and showed a high similarity with the UK strain (AF105220.1).

question: In dairy cattle, mid-diaphyseal bone geometry and strength indices are evaluated in the metacarpus and humerus across age cohorts, including 24-month-old animals, while liveweight increases. Which interpretations correctly reflect expected anatomical and biomechanical differences between these bones? Select all correct options.
A: A reduced metacarpal response to each additional kilogram of liveweight in 24-month-old cattle is consistent with earlier maturity of distal limb bones after longitudinal growth has largely ceased.
B: Absence of an age interaction for humeral bone parameters can indicate that the humerus retains capacity for growth or adaptive change at 24 months relative to the more distal metacarpus.
C: A larger stress–strain index in the humerus is compatible with greater mid-diaphyseal loading, including torsional forces transmitted through surrounding muscles during locomotion.
D: Because cattle are cursorial animals exposed to high strain rates during routine locomotion, management on hill properties would be expected to consistently increase metacarpal bone strength.
Contextual materials: Bone minimises strain such as that generated by increased bodyweight by changing content and geometry (size). However, as the animal reaches mature height and longitudinal bone growth ceases the expectation is there will be a decrease in the magnitude of the bone response to increasing live weight. This was observed in the age interaction in the metacarpus with the 24-month-old cohort demonstrating a two to three-fold reduction in the bone response for each kg increase in liveweight. Cattle are not cursorial animals and thus most locomotion is at low velocities (strain rate). Within commercial farming systems even management on hill properties did not appear to provide sufficient strain to induce an increase in bone strength. In contrast, bone parameters in the humerus did not have an age interaction, which implies that the humerus was still capable of growth at 24 months in these cattle. This finding agrees with the pattern of bone maturity described by where bones in the distal limb in the cow, such as the metacarpus, mature earlier than bones in proximal limb, such as the humerus. Differences in bone response to increases in liveweight is also a result of differences in the anatomical location of the bone and therefore differences in the direction and magnitude of the mechanical forces. The larger stress–strain index in the humerus demonstrates that at the mid-diaphysis, the humerus is subjected to a much larger force than in the metacarpus. The metacarpus undergoes compressional forces from stance resulting in a low strain rate. Whereas in the humerus, torsional forces are placed on bone via surrounding muscles during locomotion.

question: In contrast-enhanced CT evaluation of articular cartilage in the equine carpus, which statements correctly describe the expected anatomic and imaging relationships? Select all correct options.
A: Articular cartilage is not directly conspicuous on nonenhanced CT and is assessed indirectly after contrast outlines the joint space.
B: The antebrachiocarpal joint has a wide dorsal recess, relatively large range of motion, and greater cartilaginous surface area than more distal carpal compartments.
C: Cartilage visibility generally improves from proximal to distal because the distal carpal joints have larger capsular recesses and greater mobility.
D: The carpometacarpal region has flatter articular surfaces, tight joint capsules, minimal motion, and thinner cartilage, contributing to poorer distal cartilage visibility.
Contextual materials: Cartilage was only visualized indirectly after injection of contrast enhancement. Overall, the visibility of the cartilage in contrastenhanced scans was slightly better in MDCT than in CBCT scans, but decreased from proximal to distal in both modalities. The joint capsule of the ACJ therefore has a wide dorsal recessus and has the greatest range of motion and thus cartilaginous surface area. Further distally is the MCJ, which contributes less to the range of motion of the carpus and is less voluminous. The articulating osseous structures of the CMCJ, the bones of the distal/metacarpal row of the carpal joint, and the metacarpal bones, ofer flatter joint surfaces. These are tight joints with a narrow joint capsule and therefore almost no room for joint movement. These morphological particularities together with the fact of thinner cartilage in the distal joint compartments explain the poorer visibility of articular cartilage in distal carpal aspects.

question: In a microbiota survey of healthy rainbow trout mucosal sites, gill samples show high Verrucomicrobiota abundance driven mainly by Candidatus Piscichlamydia; Candidatus Branchiomonas and Flavobacterium are also detected in gills, while Candidatus Piscichlamydia and Candidatus Branchiomonas are absent from environmental water samples and occur only at lower abundance in the oropharyngeal cavity. Which interpretations are supported by these findings? Select all correct options.
A: Detection of Flavobacterium at the genus level in healthy gills is sufficient to diagnose bacterial cold water disease without lower-level taxonomic or functional resolution.
B: Candidatus Branchiomonas may be present as part of the normal gill commensal microbiota in healthy rainbow trout despite being considered a potential pathogen.
C: Lower-abundance occurrence of gill-associated genera in the oropharyngeal cavity is plausibly explained by anatomical proximity to the gills rather than by detection in the surrounding water.
D: High Candidatus Piscichlamydia abundance in ventral anterior skin definitively proves systemic dissemination from the bloodstream to the skin.
Contextual materials: The remaining examined mucosal organs showed lower inter-individual variation. For instance, the high abundance of the phylum Verrucomicrobiota in the branchial epithelium was primarily due to the genus Candidatus Piscichlamydia. In agreement with our results, Bellec et al. described Candidatus Piscichlamydia and Candidatus Branchiomonas as the most dominant genera in the gills of rainbow trout, while they were absent in the water community. Similarly, we did not find either of these genera in any of the environmental samples, whereas they were present at lower abundances in the OP cavity, likely due to its proximity to the gills. In addition, the high abundance of Candidatus Piscichlamydia in the VA skin, which accounts for the high abundance of Verrucomicrobiota in this region, may be attributed to the water outflow from the gills to this region of the skin. Regarding this hypothesis, even though many common taxa are usually found between the gills and the skin, to our knowledge, no previous studies have compared the gills with diferent skin regions along the dorsal-ventral and anterior-posterior axes, which would be necessary to validate this hypothesis. Concerning Candidatus Branchiomonas, Brown et al. reported it as the most abundant genus in the gills of rainbow trout. Upon observing that the fish were in a healthy state, both Brown et al. and Bellec et al. concluded that even though Candidatus Branchiomonas may be considered as a potential pathogen, it is part of the gill commensal microbiota of rainbow trout, in line with our results. Similarly, many studies have also noted the presence of Flavobacterium as a typical member of rainbow trout gills, even though some representatives of this genus have been described as the etiologic agent of bacterial cold water disease in rainbow trout. These findings underscore the critical need for complementary omics-based and/or conventional approaches to resolve bacterial taxonomy at lower levels and to fully understand the host-microbe interactions.

question: In calves undergoing surgical management of urachal disease, laparoscopy may require more time for the urachal resection step than conventional open surgery. Which statements correctly explain or interpret this difference? Select all correct options.
A: The longer resection step indicates that laparoscopy is unsuitable for urachal intervention in calves and cannot reliably achieve complete resection.
B: Laparoscopic access to the urachus is relatively indirect because the structure is located ventrally between the umbilical arteries rather than immediately exposed in the operative field.
C: The time difference is best explained by the urachus being a freely suspended dorsal abdominal structure that is easier to visualize laparoscopically than through an open approach.
D: Identification and manipulation of the urachus during laparoscopy can be difficult because surrounding tissues may obscure it, requiring careful tissue divulsion around the duct.
Contextual materials: Te surgical time for urachal resection in laparoscopy was longer than that in conventional open surgery because access to the urachus in laparoscopy was not direct, similar to the access to the umbilical vein. Te urachus lies in the ventral region of the abdomen, between the umbilical arteries, and is enveloped by tissues that make its identifcation and manipulation difcult (not detected during laparoscopic visualization). For satisfactory intervention in the urachus, it is important to perform tissue divulsion around the duct, a procedure that requires a skilled laparoscopist and may have infuenced the surgical time of this stage, although not greatly and not afecting the fnal surgical time. In general, urachal resection was achieved in all the animals in laparoscopy, which was shown to be an efcient technique for urachal interventions, both from a therapeutic and a diagnostic perspective. Considerable advances have already been achieved in the use of laparoscopy in urachal conditions.

question: In a pancreatic histomorphometry study of preweaning yak calves fed three forage-source diets (OP, AP, and AOP), mean area shares were reported as follows; different superscript letters within a row indicate a statistically significant difference at p < 0.05: endocrine component—OP 0.049ᵇ, AP 0.047ᵇ, AOP 0.037ᵃ; exocrine portion—OP 0.87ᵇ, AP 0.91ᵃ, AOP 0.93ᵃ; endocrine-to-exocrine area ratio—OP 0.06ᵇ, AP 0.05ᵇ, AOP 0.04ᵃ. Which interpretations are supported by these data? Select all correct options.
A: AOP had the highest endocrine-to-exocrine area ratio, indicating relative enlargement of endocrine tissue compared with OP and AP.
B: The endocrine pancreatic share showed significant stepwise separation among all three groups, with OP greater than AP and AP greater than AOP.
C: OP and AP did not differ significantly in endocrine pancreatic share, and both were significantly greater than AOP.
D: AOP had a significantly greater exocrine pancreatic share than OP, while AP was not significantly different from AOP for this measure.
Contextual materials:
As shown in Table 3, the AOP group’s total area ratio of the pancreas exocrine portion was substantially greater than that of the OP group’s $( p < 0 . 0 5 )$ . question: When interpreting 3-dimensional CT reconstructions of the skulls of an adult turtle and a green iguana, which statements correctly distinguish the relationships of the frontal and prefrontal bones? Select all correct options.
A: In the adult turtle, the frontal bone contacts the prefrontal bone rostrally, the postorbital bone laterally, and the parietal bone caudally, while being excluded from the orbit.
B: In the green iguana, the prefrontal bone contacts the nasal bone rostromedially, the lacrimal bone rostrolaterally, and the frontal bone caudomedially.
C: In the green iguana, the frontal bone directly contacts the postorbital bone laterally because no postfrontal bone intervenes between them.
D: In the adult turtle, paired lacrimal bones in the lateral orbital region separate the frontal bone from the postorbital bone.
Contextual materials: In these species, the frontal bone shows a flat shape and lies in the anterior part of the skull (Figures 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 10). The rostral VR turtle reconstruction showed a clear view of the prefrontal and frontal bone junctions (caudomedially). Therefore, the frontal bone contacts the prefrontal bone (rostrally), the postorbital bone (laterally), and the parietal bone (caudally) (Figures 2, 3 and 5). As our animals were adults, we could observe how this bone was excluded from the orbit. The VR and MIP images of the green iguana showed that the prefrontal bone contacts rostromedially with the nasal bone, rostrolaterally with the lacrimal bone (paired small bones located in the lateral region of the orbit observed only in the iguana), and caudomedially with the frontal bone (Figures 7, 8 and 10). The frontal bone is broad and forms a major component of the skull roof, contributing to the dorsal border of the orbit. It meets the prefrontal bone rostrolaterally, the postfrontal bone caudolaterally, and the parietal bone caudally (Figures 7, 8 and 10). Laterally, it is differentiated from the postorbital by the postfrontal bone.

question: In an air-liquid-interface culture model of bovine oviduct epithelial cells, prolonged cortisol exposure is associated with epithelial disorganization, loss of ciliation, cytoplasmic vacuolation, expansion of secretory-cell areas, trends toward reduced TP53 and DDB2 expression, and development of multilayers in many cultures. Which interpretations are biologically consistent with these findings? Select all correct options.
A: Reduced ciliation would be expected to impair transport of gametes and early embryos, and could plausibly relate to reduced ESR1-mediated estrogen signaling that normally supports oviductal ciliogenesis.
B: Reduced TP53 and DDB2 expression would indicate strengthened DNA damage response capacity and a lower likelihood of glucocorticoid-associated tumor-promoting effects.
C: Expansion of secretory-cell areas may be concerning because it can resemble early precursor-type lesions associated with oviduct-derived high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
D: Loss of epithelial homogeneity and multilayer formation are compatible with impaired monolayer-dependent oviduct function and may be promoted by reduced expression of extracellular matrix components such as FBLN2 that help maintain basement membrane integrity.
Contextual materials: Te prolonged cortisol stimulation in the bovine OEC model resulted in disorganization of the oviduct epithelium, contrasting with our previous observations in the porcine model. Te adverse efects on morphology in BOEC cultures varied among animals, ranging from mild to severe, and was marked by a loss of ciliation and an increase in cytoplasmic vacuoles observed in all animals. Reduction in ciliated cells would directly impair the transport of gametes and early embryos within the oviduct in vivo. Tis decrease might be attributed to the downregulation of ESR1 caused by the chronic cortisol stimulation, as the estrogen signalling is known to promote ciliogenesis in the oviduct. On the other hand, the increased areas of secretory cells mimicked the earliest precursor lesions of oviduct-derived highgrade serous ovarian cancer. Furthermore, we noted a diminished expression trend of the tumor suppressor TP53, along with its downstream gene DDB2, crucial for DNA damage response, following a 3-week cortisol treatment. Tis fnding aligns with a previous study on chronic restraint stress in mice, illustrating that elevated glucocorticoids mediate the attenuation of p53 function and promotes tumorigenesis. More than 50% of the ALI-BOEC cultures additionally exhibited a loss of homogeneity and the development of multilayers, a phenomenon evident as early as 1 week after cortisol stimulation. Te functionality of the oviduct tissue is known to rely on the monolayer structure, and disorganisation of the epithelial layer is associated with diseases such as cancer. Te formation of multilayers following cortisol exposure may be attributed to the downregulation of extracellular matrix components, such as FBLN2, which plays a crucial role in preserving the basement membrane integrity of epithelium, and its reduced expression is linked to abnormal cell growth.

question: In a bovine IVF laboratory using time-lapse monitoring, abnormal early cleavage patterns are being evaluated in zygotes from clinically healthy cows and cows with inflammatory or combined disease. Which statements correctly interpret mechanisms or management implications of these cleavage abnormalities? Select all correct options.
A: Direct cleavage is generally interpreted as a normal morphokinetic variant in cattle and is unrelated to subsequent embryonic arrest or transfer decisions.
B: Direct cleavage can arise from multiple pronuclei or erroneous pronuclear migration, and inflammatory follicular conditions may contribute by disrupting oocyte spindle or microtubule organization needed for pronuclear apposition.
C: If all IVF groups are fertilized with semen from a single bull and the same semen batch, true group differences in reverse cleavage incidence may be difficult to detect because reverse cleavage is strongly influenced by male-factor semen characteristics.
D: Although reverse cleavage has been associated with failure to reach the blastocyst stage in some bovine studies, embryos showing reverse cleavage should not necessarily be discarded immediately because some may still develop to blastocysts.
Contextual materials: Recently, it has been shown that multi pronuclei and migration error of pronuclei are the primary reasons for direct cleavage in cattle. Using TLM we were able to observe a higher probability of direct cleavage in zygotes of cows with combined and inflammatory disease. This might be due to the negative efects of intrafollicular inflammatory agents on oocyte spindle assembly, considering that abnormalities in oocyte microtubule positioning lead to failure in pronuclei apposition. As direct cleavage was previously associated with embryonic arrest in cattle, it would be interesting to analyze the pregnancy rate after transfer of embryos from diseased cows produced in this study. In human medicine, direct cleavage embryos are not recommended for day 3 transfers, but can be transferred if they reach blastocyst stage in culture. Reverse cleavage has also been reported in bovine embryos in recent studies with an incidence of 11%–17% and its occurrence prevented the zygotes from reaching the blastocyst stage. The occurrence of reverse cleavage is mainly attributed to the male factor, as semen characteristics at fertilization are strongly correlated to abnormal patterns of cell divison. This might also explain why we could not observe any diference in the incidence of reverse cleavage in this study, as only semen from one bull and from the same batch was used for IVF. However, our observations showed that zygotes with reverse cleavage can still reach the blastocyst stage, and therefore should not be removed from culture at early stages.

question: In a dog undergoing regional anesthesia of the ventral cervical plexus, which statements correctly describe the relevant anatomy and sensory distribution? Select all correct options.
A: The plexus is formed mainly by ventral branches of C1 through C4, sometimes including C5, and these branches course in the interfascial plane between the omotransversarius and the deep cervical muscles.
B: The ventral branch of C1 is the principal cutaneous source to the base of the external ear and the convex surface of the auricle.
C: The ventral branch of C2 gives rise to the great auricular and transverse cervical nerves, contributing sensory supply to regions including the parotid area, base of the external ear, laryngeal region, and intermandibular space.
D: The proximal lateroventral cervical dermatomes are supplied predominantly by dorsal branches of C2 and C3 after they pass superficial to the omotransversarius.
Contextual materials: In dogs, the ventral cervical plexus is composed of ventral branches originating from the first (C1) to the fourth (C4) and sometimes the fifth (C5) cervical spinal nerves. These branches traverse the interfascial plane between the omotransversarius muscle and the deep muscles of the neck, surrounded by the deep cervical fascia. The omotransversarius muscle is a longitudinal and substantial muscular band that is flattened on the lateral side of the neck and extends from the shoulder surface to the atlantoidea region. The ventral branch of C1 is connected to the vagosympathetic trunk and the accessory nerve, and it does not provide cutaneous innervation. The ventral branch of C2 divides into the great auricular and transverse cervical nerves, which are responsible for innervating the parotid region, the base of the external ear, the skin of the convex face of the auricle, as well as the laryngeal region and intermandibular space, respectively. The ventral branches of C3–C5 innervate the hypaxial cervical muscles and provide sensory innervation to the soft tissues in the region. The dermatomes in the proximal half of the neck’s lateroventral region are innervated by the cutaneous branches of the ventral branches of the C2 and C3 cervical nerves (Figure 1).

question: In a canine histologic assessment of leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) membranes, the biomaterial is evaluated by blood-cell distribution, staining characteristics, and semiquantitative layer features. Which statements correctly describe the expected histologic organization and assessment findings? Select all correct options.
A: A five-zone arrangement may be identified, progressing from an erythrocyte-rich layer through mixed and leukocyte-rich layers to platelet-rich and fibrin-dominant layers.
B: The fibrin network is expected to stain intensely red and contain the highest density of erythrocytes in the membrane.
C: Platelets and platelet aggregates are typically absent from the organized membrane layers and are not distinguishable histologically from the fibrin network.
D: Most specimens show a well-demarcated zonal pattern, heavy cellular aggregation in the cell-layer zone, and more than 10 cell layers at the border.
Contextual materials: Histological analysis of the L-PRF membranes showed that there were five zones or layers, based on the distribution and density of blood cells in this biomaterial (Figure 2). The first layer was composed primarily of erythrocytes, followed by a transitional zone of leukocytes, erythrocytes, and platelets, a layer of leukocytes, a layer of platelets, and then a layer of fibrin. Erythrocytes were stained red, whereas platelets and platelet aggregates were stained dark pink. The fibrin network was almost white and contained few cells. Semiquantitative assessment of membrane histology showed the following results: (1) Zone layers in the membrane: a well-demarcated pattern (score 1) in 95% of the specimens; (2) Number of cell layers at border: the percentage of more than 10 cell layers (score 1) was observed in 92% of the specimens; (3) Aggregation of cells in the cell layer zone: the L-PRF membranes showed heavy aggregation (score 1) in the 90% of the specimens; (4) Cell border morphology: all the membranes (100%) showed very clear cell wall morphology.

question: In an embryonic ZW goose leg-muscle developmental series from E15 to E23, histology shows myofibers changing from small, loosely arranged profiles to larger polygonal fibers in tightly packed fascicles, with reduced interstitial tissue. Pax7 immunolabeling of satellite/myogenic precursor cells declines from about 22% at E15 to about 5% at E23, with a particularly sharp decrease by E18. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: The histologic transition is consistent with progressive myofiber maturation and increasing fascicular organization during embryonic muscle development.
B: The decline in Pax7-positive cells suggests that many myogenic precursors exit the proliferative pool and incorporate into developing myofibers, while a smaller reserve population remains.
C: The sharp E15-to-E18 reduction in Pax7-positive cells supports interpreting E18 as a transition point from proliferative expansion toward hypertrophic maturation.
D: The reduced interstitial tissue and lower Pax7-positive fraction indicate persistence of an expanded undifferentiated satellite-cell pool through E23.
Contextual materials: The present study delineates the morphological, cellular and mo lecular underpinnings of embryonic leg muscle development in the ZW goose. Our integrated analysis revealed a well-defined developmental trajectory characterized by progressive myofiber maturation and dy namic remodeling of the SMSC pool. Histologically, myofibers transi tioned from small, loosely arranged structures into large, polygonal fibers organized into tightly packed fascicles between E15F and E23F, accompanied by a marked reduction in interstitial tissue—a pattern consistent with previous observations in other goose breed. Concurrently, the proportion of Pax7⁺ satellite cells decreased progressively from 22 % at E15 to 5 % at E23, indicating that most myoblasts exit the cell cycle and incorporate into developing myofibers, thereby establishing a quiescent reserve for postnatal muscle growth and regeneration. The sharp decline in Pax7⁺ cell frequency between E15 and E18 coincides with a phase of rapid myofiber hyper plasia previously described in poultry, suggesting that E18 represents a critical transition from proliferative expansion to hy pertrophic maturation. Collectively, these stage-specific morphological and cellular changes provide a robust temporal framework for inter preting transcriptomic dynamics and identifying optimal intervention windows for enhancing muscle yield in meat-type geese.

question: A dog has a focal exophytic proliferative mass arising from the chorioallantois and composed only of fetal placental tissue with trophoblastic involvement. Histology shows trophoblastic cell piling, numerous mitoses, moderate pleomorphism, prominent single or multiple nucleoli, and megalocytosis, with no identifiable external stimulus that would explain a localized reactive proliferation. Which statements correctly support interpreting this lesion as a benign trophoblastic neoplasm rather than hypertrophy, hyperplasia, or hamartoma? Select all correct options.
A: Autonomous proliferation without evidence of an external stimulus favors neoplasia over hypertrophy or hyperplasia.
B: A focal exophytic growth pattern with cellular piling, mitotic activity, pleomorphism, nucleolar prominence, and megalocytosis supports a neoplastic process.
C: The presence of only fetal tissue within the mass, rather than normal fetal-maternal placental structures, supports focal hyperplasia as the most likely diagnosis.
D: A hamartoma is, by definition, a non-neoplastic transformation, so classifying the lesion as a hamartoma would not support a diagnosis of placental chorioadenoma.
Contextual materials: The proliferative mass presented in this report had features consistent with a benign neoplastic process arising in the chorioallantois and involving placental trophoblasts, namely a placental chorioadenoma. Histological features suggestive of neoplasia include the focal exophytic growth, trophoblastic cell piling, high mitotic rate, moderate cellular pleomorphism, prominent single or multiple nucleoli and megalocytosis. Proliferative lesions can be hypertrophic, hyperplastic, or neoplastic. Although grossly hypertrophy, hyperplasia and neoplasia can look similar, their diferences lie in the underlying initiation factors, the type of tissue involved and the microscopic characteristics of the cells and tissue. Hypertrophic and hyperplastic changes are a response to some specific stimulation external to the afected cells and tissues. In some cases, the stimulus is not obvious, but it remains true that these proliferative changes are controlled and not autonomous. In contrast, neoplastic changes (whether benign or malignant) are autonomous and not related to stimulation external to the afected cells. In this case, the lack of any evidence of a stimulus that could have led to focal hyperplasia, the presence of only fetal tissue and no fetal-maternal structures, as in the normal canine placenta, within the mass further support that this is a neoplastic, rather than a hyperplastic process. Gestational neoplastic transformation of trophoblastic cells is a known entity in humans, however, in veterinary medicine, the only trophoblastic neoplasms that have been described were mola hydatidosa in cows. A proliferative placental mass of trophoblastic origin was described in a bitch with some similarities to the mass presented here. That study, however, reported the mass as a placental hamartoma which, by definition, is a non-neoplastic transformation. To date, other case reports on gestational placental neoplasms in domestic animal species described a stem cell tumor, a teratoma, and a mixed germ cell tumor.

question: In canine carpal anatomy, the term canalis carpi is best reserved for a true, well-defined tunnel rather than any space deep to superficial retinacular fascia. Which statements correctly characterize this anatomically restricted canine canalis carpi? Select all correct options.
A: It is formed by the superficial part of the flexor retinaculum alone, which creates a true canal containing all major digital flexor tendons and palmar neurovascular structures.
B: It is a non-distensible, oval space bounded palmarly by the deep part of the flexor retinaculum and dorsally by the common palmar ligament over the palmar carpal bones.
C: Its contents include the tendons of the flexor digitorum profundus and interflexorius muscle, together with the median nerve and median artery and vein.
D: It is anatomically equivalent to a defined tunnel beneath the extensor retinaculum on the dorsal aspect of the carpus.
Contextual materials: In this study, the canalis carpi in dogs was described as a non-distensible and welldefined oval space delimitated palmarly by the deep part of the flexor retinaculum, laterally by a thin fibrous septum, dorsally by the common palmar ligament that covers the palmar region of the carpal bones, and medially by the fixations of the fused antebrachial fascia to the deep part of the flexor retinaculum and the common palmar ligament. It contained the tendons of the flexor digitorum profundus and the interflexorius muscle, as well as the nervus medianus and the arteria and vena mediana. The inconsistency found in the literature is probably related to the non-differentiation between the superficial and deep parts of the flexor retinaculum. Dyce et al., Evans and de Lahunta, and Turan et al. made their descriptions assuming that the flexor retinaculum was only constituted by the superficial part, which led to the inclusion of other tendons and neurovascular structures inside the hypothetical canalis carpi.
