Interestingly, amongst infected lambs, Prevotella was signifcantly associated with unvaccinated animals; whilst it must be noted that, unlike in our previous study, the efects of vaccine administration were minimal in both the 2017 and 2018 trial, it is tempting to speculate that vaccination against T. circumcincta might prevent a signifcant expansion of populations of Prevotella via the establishment of lower infection burdens compared to unvaccinated animals. Tese data support the hypothesis that, although infection is a major driver of microbial composition remodelling, vaccination may further reshape the ruminant microbial gut composition by reducing worm survival.

question: In assessing parasite-related confounding and disease management in trout held in an Australian freshwater hatchery, which statements are correct? Select all correct options.
A: Some parasites of trout can alter host behaviour, so confirming parasite absence is important when interpreting behavioural observations.
B: Flow-through hatchery systems using surrounding water sources are generally easier to control for water temperature and incoming infectious agents than closed or more controlled systems.
C: Chemical immersion treatments used in parasite management may include sodium percarbonate or formalin.
D: Temperature can shift parasite community composition; diplomonads may be more abundant at very cold temperatures around 1–5°C, whereas ciliophorans are associated with warmer conditions around 16–20°C.
Contextual materials: The presence of parasites, particularly those with the ability to manipulate host behaviour, is a well-documented aspect of trout ecology. Several parasites utilise trout as their intermediate hosts, creating a dynamic relationship that can influence the behaviour of these fish. Interestingly, certain parasites, like Eustrongylides larvae, have been identified as common parasites of trout in Australian freshwater systems. However, we found no parasites in our fish and therefore no parasitic influences on the behaviour exhibited by the subjects. The absence of parasites in the sample subjects is most likely due to the water quality at the Gaden Hatchery, though treatment and prevention practices can also significantly reduce the incidence of disease and parasite infection. Parasite management often relies on chemical therapy immersions, generally of either sodium percarbonate or formalin. Water temperature and the chemical therapies used influence the prevalence of parasites and the types of parasites found, with some parasites, such as diplomonad species, showing higher abundances at temperatures between 1 and $5 ^ { \circ } C ,$ whereas ciliophoran species prefer warmer water temperatures of 16 to 20 ◦C. Another consideration for hatchery management is the water source used throughout the hatchery, with flow-through systems that use a surrounding water source, harder to manage in terms of regulating water temperature and the infectious agents that come through the system.

question: In anisakid nematode developmental staging, investigators compare larvae that emerge naturally from eggs with larvae mechanically forced from eggs shortly before hatching. Naturally hatched larvae may show multiple cuticular coverings, including a loose sheath and a tighter covering, with exsheathment beginning soon after hatching; some earlier reports designated the emerging larva as L3 because it resembled infective L3 and appeared to carry a loose second-stage sheath. Which interpretations are justified? Select all correct options.
A: The observation of cuticular remnants associated with the intra-egg moult can support interpreting the naturally emerging free-living larva as a second-stage larva rather than necessarily as L3.
B: The presence of an oesophagus, ventriculus, intestine, and a putative excretory cell is by itself sufficient to prove that the newly hatched larva is L3.
C: An L3 designation based on a loose sheath plus a tight body-fitting cuticle depends critically on correctly assigning those cuticles to specific moults, so misidentification of cuticle layers can alter the staging conclusion.
D: Mechanical extrusion of larvae from eggs just before spontaneous hatching is equivalent to natural hatching and eliminates ambiguity about which larval stage normally emerges.
Contextual materials: Anisakis pegrefi egg development and hatching cascade aligns with that described in soil-transmitted helminths, although the cues for the process initiations remain elusive. Despite previous reports that L3 is the stage in anisakids and H. aduncum that emerges from the egg, all hatched larvae observed here clearly showed two cuticle sheaths, one tightly enveloping the larvae and the second loosely enwrapping the larvae, whose exsheathment started immediately posthatching. Te L1 cuticle remained within the egg after the hatching of L2, but this is not always clearly discernible. It is important to highlight that Køie et al. observed that live larvae, forced out of eggs in seawater by coverslip pressure shortly before spontaneous hatching, were surrounded by the thin cuticle of the L1. In contrast, infective larvae from naturally hatched eggs were loosely ensheathed in the thick cuticle of the L2. Based on this, Køie et al. concluded that the larva that emerges from the egg is L3 rather than the L2, as previously observed. Køie et al. observed a loose cuticle sheet of the L2, implying that the tight one ftting the larval body is L3 cuticle, and consequently designated the larva as L3. Tis hypothesis has been retained in successive studies, such as the one describing A. simplex hatching, where similarly only a single ensheathed cuticle was observed. In contrast, two ensheathed and one cuticle on the larval body were discernible in Ascaris lumbricoides L3 hatching from the egg. Adroher et al. and Vales-Vega et al. concluded that L3 of H. aduncum and Contracaecum multipapillatum s.l. also hatched from eggs, based on a strong similarity of the hatched stage to the infective L3, namely, the presence of the excretory cell, oesophagus, ventriculus and intestine. However, Vales-Vega et al. reported that the excretory gland cell in C. multipapillatum s.l. was visible only after approximately 25 days in culture. Using confocal and conventional microscopy, in the present work a distinctively larger cell situated in the proximal second third of the larval body was observed already 72 h posthatching, but it is speculative whether the cell indeed develops into the excretory gland cell without the use of cell-specifc markers. Overall, our observation supports that of Smith and Wootten, who emphasised that “the free-living larva which emerges from the egg is apparently a second stage and ensheathed in the cast cuticle of the frst moult which evidently takes place within the egg”.

question: In recently weaned beef calves with diarrhea, fecal examination identifies Buxtonella sulcata in many animals, with some calves also harboring Eimeria spp., Toxocara vitulorum, or Moniezia spp. The calves have recently begun consuming roughage and green fodder, and the feeding regimen changed abruptly. Which statements are valid interpretations of the parasitologic and management findings? Select all correct options.
A: Abrupt dietary change would be expected to reduce B. sulcata multiplication and virulence by stabilizing digestive tract pH, making it an unlikely contributor to diarrhea.
B: Contaminated roughage or green fodder may expose calves to oribatid mites, which serve as intermediate hosts for anoplocephalid cestodes such as Moniezia.
C: If single B. sulcata infections are more common than B. sulcata coinfections, this supports considering B. sulcata as a possible primary contributor to diarrhea rather than only an incidental coinfection.
D: A high fecal cyst burden of B. sulcata can be interpreted as increased protozoal invasion that may accelerate intestinal passage and contribute to diarrhea.
Contextual materials: At this stage of post-weaning age, the calves begin to eat roughage and green fodders, which may be contaminated with the orbatide mite (intermediate host of anoplocephalids), considered the source of Moniezia infection. The study of the association between B. sulcata and other parasitic infections in this study revealed that the most common pattern of parasitic co-infection was a double infection with B. sulcata and Eimeria species and of B. sulcata with T. vitulorum. Meanwhile, single infections with B. sulcata (35 case) were more frequent than B. sulcata coinfections with other parasites, indicating that B. sulcata might be the cause of diarrhea. In fact, the number of protozoan pathogens in the feces was high (≤500 cyst per gram), which reflected an increase of B. sulcata invasion. This could contribute to the acceleration of alimentary content passage in the intestine, resulting in diarrhea. Moreover, a sudden change in the feeding system afects the digestive tract pH, and an incorrect diet causes diarrhea in calves owing to the multiplication of B. sulcata and the enhancement of the parasite virulence. Therefore, B. sulcata is a frequent cause of diarrhea in calves. However, the association of bacterial, viral, and fungal infections with B. sulcata remains to be investigated.

question: A wildlife parasitology surveillance project in East Asian ungulates detects several Theileria taxa by molecular testing. Which statements correctly interpret known host associations and pathogenic significance for these parasites? Select all correct options.
A: T. capreoli, originally described from roe deer, is generally regarded as a benign parasite of wild cervids and has been detected in multiple deer species.
B: T. luwenshuni and T. uilenbergi are well recognized as highly pathogenic Theileria of sheep and goats, but their pathogenicity in wild ungulates remains uncertain.
C: Finding a Theileria genotype in takin that had previously been reported from Japanese serows would be consistent with occasional detection of Theileria taxa in unexpected wild hosts.
D: Detection of T. luwenshuni or T. uilenbergi in a takin would be expected only if the animal had concurrent erythrocyte infection, because Theileria do not infect leukocytes.
Contextual materials: Theileria is tick-borne protozoa, infecting both leukocytes and erythrocytes of their vertebrate hosts. Domestic and wild animals are susceptible to diferent Theileria species, many of which are previously known to be reasonably host specific. However, increasing evidence showed that some Theileria species have been identified in unexpected hosts from diferent geographic locations, especially in wild animals. In this study, T. capreoli was identified in Himalayan goral, Reeves’ muntjac, and forest musk deer. This organism is initially described from roe deer and is considered to be a benign parasite of wild cervids; the infections have also been recorded in fallow deer, red deer, and Chinese water deer. Theileria uilenbergi and T. luwenshuni are considered to be highly pathogenic parasites of small domestic ruminants. The occurrence of these two Theileria species has been widely reported in sheep and goats from China and causes great economic losses for the livestock industry. However, there are sporadic reports of T. uilenbergi and T. luwenshuni in wild animals. To date, infection of T. luwenshuni (Theileria sp. China 1) was observed in a few Chinese water deer and roe deer from South Korea, roe deer, sika deer, and red deer from China, while T. uilenbergi has been detected in red deer, sika deer, and Reeves’ muntjac from China. The present study constitutes the first evidence of T. luwenshuni and T. uilenbergi infections in takins. As mentioned above, these two Theileria parasites are high pathogenic for sheep and goats; however, their pathogenicity for wild animals is still unclear, which warrants further investigation. Moreover, a potential novel Theileria parasite (Theileria sp. T4) was identified in takin from this study that has been previously reported in Capricornis crispus (AB012201) and Japanese serows (AB602881).

question: A molecular epidemiologic survey of Cryptosporidium spp. in beef calves in the Republic of Korea assessed seasonal patterns, species occurrence, and weather-related risk factors. Which statements are valid interpretations of such findings? Select all correct options.
A: Seasonal species distribution may differ by Cryptosporidium species, with C. parvum predominating in fall and C. ryanae predominating in summer.
B: Heavy summer precipitation can plausibly increase calf exposure by promoting overcrowding, preventing floor drying, improving oocyst survival, and facilitating spread through surface water or groundwater.
C: A significant association between season and Cryptosporidium occurrence would rule out farm-level factors such as breeding density, humidity, temperature, and precipitation as contributors.
D: If most calves are born from spring to summer, increasing calf density and exposure to oocysts shed by older calves could contribute to greater susceptibility from summer into fall.
Contextual materials: In the present study, we found a seasonal association in the occurrence of Cryptosporidium spp. Our results revealed that season had a significant efect on the occurrence of C. parvum and C. ryanae: C. parvum dominance in fall, and C. ryanae dominance in summer. However, this finding difers from previous results, which reported that the occurrence of C. bovis was dominant in summer, whereas that of C. parvum was dominant in spring and winter. According to another study performed in the ROK, season and the occurrence of C. parvum were not associated. The relationship between season and the occurrence of Cryptosporidium spp. remains unclear, but it seems that their occurrence may vary depending on the farm situation in each country. Notably, levels of sunlight, temperature, humidity, and precipitation, as well as breeding density, may play a role in this variation. One possibility is that calves are mostly born from spring to summer in the ROK, which increases the density of calves within the herd and makes calves more susceptible to Cryptosporidium spp. oocysts shed by older calves that were born earlier in the season. Especially, in the ROK, it rains heavily in summer. Heavy rain results in the overcrowding of animals and hampers the drying of the floor, thereby increasing the survival of Cryptosporidium oocysts. Our results showed that precipitation in the preceding month was significantly associated with the occurrence of Cryptosporidium spp. $( P = 0 . 0 1 5 )$ (data not shown). As previously mentioned, precipitation is highest in summer, followed by that in fall, spring, and winter. Cryptosporidium spp. oocysts are likely to easily spread through rivers or groundwater to surrounding farms due to heavy rain, which increases the opportunity for calves to be exposed. Owing to the long survival of Cryptosporidium spp. oocysts, susceptible calves with lower immunity are more frequently present from summer to fall. These results suggest that precipitation may act as an important factor in the occurrence of cryptosporidiosis. Our findings provide new insights on the seasonal occurrence of Cryptosporidium spp., and hence, their control.

question: In surveillance for Toxoplasma gondii in slaughtered sheep, investigators compare serologic assays such as MAT or ELISA with PCR/qPCR performed on small heart or skeletal muscle samples. They observe low-to-moderate Cohen’s kappa values, with many seropositive sheep lacking detectable parasite DNA in the tested tissue and only rare PCR-positive results among seronegative sheep. Which interpretations are scientifically justified? Select all correct options.
A: Low agreement can be driven by poor recovery of parasite DNA from the tested tissue of seropositive sheep rather than by serology necessarily being nonspecific.
B: Low kappa values prove that the heart is not a biologically relevant tissue for T. gondii cyst localization in sheep and should be excluded from diagnostic sampling.
C: Patchy distribution of tissue cysts and a small amount of sampled muscle or heart can reduce the probability of detecting parasite genetic material.
D: Negative serology may be more useful for predicting absence of detectable parasite DNA in heart or skeletal muscle than positive serology is for predicting PCR positivity.
Contextual materials: A similar level of agreement (MAT and PCR) was reported from Iranian researchers who tested blood and hearts from sheep sampled at a slaughterhouse (kappa = 0.33). Mazuz et al. obtained an even lower correlation testing 1.5 square centimeters from sheep’s heart (kappa calculated from the reported data is 0.08). However, Hamilton at al. found a moderate level of agreement between seropositivity (ELISA) and the presence of DNA (qPCR) in sheep heart (kappa calculated from the provided data = 0.67). This tendency to a low agreement could be mainly due to low values of recovery rate of T. gondii DNA in seropositive sheep. Indeed, all of the mentioned studies reported a recovery rate from muscle or heart that varied between 11% and 65% in the positive sheep. As explained in the previous paragraph, an uneven distribution of the tissue cysts in the carcass or in the muscle as well as a low amount of tested sample could impact on the likelihood of detecting genetic material of the parasite. On contrary, serological tests appear to be good predictors of negative muscle since, like in our study, the finding of the parasite DNA in heart or skeleton muscle from seronegative animals is an infrequent event.

question: In molecular epidemiologic studies of equine piroplasmosis agents related to Theileria equi, which statements accurately describe genotype classification and interpretation of sequence data? Select all correct options.
A: The South African 18S rRNA study assigned B. equi Spain-1 and Spain-2 isolates to genotype C, placed T. equi-like horse and zebra isolates in genotype A, and established genotype E from Sudanese horse samples.
B: An 18S rRNA-based scheme recognizes five genotypes, A through E, and the genotype designated T. equi-C includes the organism described as T. haneyi.
C: The 18S rRNA gene is useful for genotyping because it is present in multiple genomic copies and contains hypervariable regions; an earlier EMA-1-based approach distinguished Florida and Pelotas genotypes.
D: Sequencing of 23 samples from grazing horses in Kyrgyzstan identified genotypes A and E, with genotype E detected more frequently, supporting coexistence of distinct T. equi genotypes in one horse population.
Contextual materials: In recent studies, it has been shown that EP agents are divided into five genotypes (A, B, C, D, and E) based on the 18S rRNA gene. Moreover, it has been reported that the T. equi-C genotype includes the species described as T. haneyi. In 2001, it was reported that T. equi has two genotypes (Florida (United States) and Pelotas (Southern Brazil) genotypes) based on the EMA-1 gene. The 18S rRNA gene has advantages in genotyping studies due to the fact that it has multiple copies in the genome and the hypervariable region is also located here. It has been used extensively in studies on this subject. Firstly, B. equi Spain 1 and B. equi Spain 2 were reported in 2003, based on the 18S rRNA gene. In another conducted in Spain in 2004, B. equi Spain 1 and B. equi Spain 2 isolates were located in the same cluster, while T. equi-like was located in a diferent cluster, thus supporting the existence of two genotypes based on two 18S rRNA genes. In a more comprehensive study conducted in South Africa in 2009, a third genotype was detected, and the genotypes up to that time were named genotypes A, B, and C. According to the study, B. equi Spain-1 and B. equi Spain-2 isolates detected from horses and T. equi isolate detected from dogs in Spain were collected under genotype A; T. equi-like isolates detected from horses in Spain and, and from zebra in South Africa were collected genotype B, and T. equi isolates detected from horses in South Africa were collected under genotype C. Following these, the presence of genotype D in horses in Sudan was revealed in 2010, and genotype E was revealed in 2012 based on previous South Korean-T. equi sequences. In this study, 23 samples were sequenced. As a result of phylogenetic analysis based on 18S rRNA gene DNA sequences, we identified two genetically distinct T. equi genotypes (A—4 samples and E—19 samples) in grazing horses from Kyrgyzstan. This is the first study that reports of T. equi and its genotypes in Kyrgyzstan. Our results confirm that diferent genotypes of T. equi coexist within the same population and the heterogeneous nature of this species, in agreement with previous studies. However, there is still a need for molecular surveys to determine the geographical distribution of the genotypes and their impact on the course of clinical infections, as well as studies on diferences in vectors.

question: In an experimental Eimeria tenella challenge study in broiler chickens, a combination anticoccidial formulation was tested at low, medium, and high doses. The high-dose group had the greatest relative body weight gain, less cecal lesion damage, lower oocyst output, and an anticoccidial index (ACI) of 169.2. For comparison, artemisinin has been reported to reduce relative body weight gain partly by suppressing feed intake, and garlic essential oil at 0.06 ml/L has been reported to have an ACI of 167.57. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: An ACI of 169.2 supports classifying the high-dose combination as having good anticoccidial efficacy when an ACI greater than 160 is used as the threshold.
B: The higher relative body weight gain of the combination formulation compared with artemisinin suggests a potential economic advantage for broiler meat production.
C: The high-dose combination’s efficacy profile is supported by concurrent improvement in growth performance, cecal lesion severity, and oocyst shedding.
D: Because garlic essential oil had an ACI of 167.57, it demonstrated stronger anticoccidial efficacy than the high-dose combination formulation.
Contextual materials: Tis study also evaluated the anticoccidial efect of gradient doses of the combination formulation. Te results found that the high-dose group had a better weight gain efect than the low- and medium-dose groups, and that the high dose efectively alleviated the cecal lesion damage caused by Eimeria tenella infection and exhibited a better oocyst output reduction efect. At the same time, the ACI of the high-dose group (169.2) was higher than that of the low- and medium-dose groups, and its high ACI (> 160.0) suggested its good anticoccidial efect. It has been reported that artemisinin exerts anticoccidial efect by inhibiting the feed intake of broilers, resulting in relatively low rBWG. Compared with artemisinin, our combination formulation showed a larger relative weight gain, indicating its advantages in terms of the economic benefts of broiler meat production. Te ACI of garlic essential oil (0.06 ml/l) has been reported to be 167.57, which is lower than that of our combination formulation, suggesting the better anticoccidial efect of our combination formulation.

question: A dairy herd is considering deep-bedded freestalls using recycled manure solids (RMS) rather than sand or straw, with hock lesion prevalence as a key welfare outcome. Which statements correctly describe mechanisms by which bedding management can influence hock lesions in lactating dairy cows? Select all correct options.
A: Increasing bedding depth can reduce hock lesion risk by cushioning cows from abrasive or hard stall bases, sometimes making depth more important than bedding material type.
B: Because RMS is less dense than sand, it may compact more readily in stalls, potentially exposing the rear curb and increasing hock lesion risk unless bedding is added frequently.
C: The relatively low dry matter content of RMS should protect hock skin because prolonged contact with moist bedding maintains skin elasticity and prevents lesion formation.
D: Cleaner lower legs in cows bedded on RMS are not necessarily protective against hock lesions, because dirt on the skin may provide some physical shielding.
Contextual materials: Management of hock lesions is challenging and it was demonstrated that usage of deep-bedding systems results in a decrease of hock lesions prevalence. Others also demonstrated that bedding depth, by mitigating the impact of abrasive or hard stall base on cows, may play a more important role for the cow welfare than the bedding type itself. Due to its large availability once a farm is equipped, RMS is of great interest since it could be used in large amount in stalls, including deep-bedded stalls. However, RMS is considerably less dense than sand, another common bedding type used in deep bedding system. Therefore, when it will be used, RMS will tend to be compressed more easily than sand, which may expose the rear curb of the stalls and cause an increase in hock lesions prevalence. The latter was indeed reported with sawdust bedding in deep-bedding systems. This potential negative impact could be attenuated with frequent addition of bedding in stalls. When compared to other bedding types, RMS may also be problematic for hock’s health in regards to its low dry matter content. Prolonged contact with wet bedding may compromise the integrity of the skin, which may then be prone to the development of lesions. Finally, in our study, we found that cows housed on RMS had cleaner lower legs than cows housed on straw. While having animals with a good hygiene level is desirable, this may put them at a greater risk of developing hock lesions. As a matter of fact, dirt could serve as a sort of protective shield for the skin.

question: When evaluating carprofen analgesic regimens for laboratory mice, which statements correctly interpret the available pharmacologic evidence? Select all correct options.
A: Use of carprofen for pain relief in rodents is off-label, even though carprofen has veterinary approvals for some clinical species in the EU and for dogs in the US.
B: A 20 mg/kg subcutaneous dose in C57Bl/6J mice is eliminated so rapidly that plasma concentrations generally fall below the estimated therapeutic threshold well before 12 hours.
C: The often-cited minimum therapeutic plasma concentration of 24.3 µg/mL in mice is an estimated threshold derived from in vitro canine blood cell COX-2 inhibition data, not a confirmed in vivo mouse therapeutic level.
D: Pharmacokinetic findings from C57Bl/6J and CD1 mice support dosing intervals of at least 12 hours for maintaining relevant plasma concentrations when medium-to-high subcutaneous doses are used.
Contextual materials: Carprofen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is commonly used in laboratory rodents to relieve pain and inflammation. It is approved for clinical use in veterinary patients in the EU (various species) and the US (dog) in multiple preparations, but the application for pain relief in rodents remains of-label. For mice, dose recommendations cover a range of approximately 2–20 mg/kg s.c. every 12–24 h, depending on the source used. In vivo therapeutic plasma levels in mice are still unknown to date. However, current literature often refers to an estimated therapeutic threshold above 24.3 µg/ml calculated from in vitro data using canine blood cells (corresponding to a carprofen concentration inhibiting 80% of COX-2 activity). Our study shows that plasma levels remain above this estimated threshold for up to 24 h in male and female C57Bl/6J mice when 20 mg/kg are injected s.c. This is in line with recent observations made in another mouse strain, i.e., female CD1 mice. The authors report a $t _ { 1 / 2 }$ of 10.2 h following s.c. injection of 20 mg/kg, matching the $t _ { 1 / 2 }$ of 8.52 h determined in the present study. Surprisingly, a somewhat shorter $t _ { 1 / 2 }$ of 6.88 h was previously reported for a sustained-release formulation (5 mg/kg s.c.) in female CD1 mice. Altogether, the comparatively slow elimination and maintenance of presumed minimal therapeutic plasma levels for at least 12 h [10 mg/kg s.c.] and up to 24 h (20 mg/kg s.c.), the present study suggest that an injection interval of ≥12 h is appropriate for achieving consistently relevant plasma levels with medium to high carprofen doses in mice of diferent strains and both sexes.

question: In a study of Eimeria detection in chicken intestinal samples, 18S rDNA next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified dominant and minority operational taxonomic units (OTUs), and species-specific quantitative PCR (qPCR) assays were used on selected samples as biological positive controls. Which interpretations are scientifically appropriate when comparing these methods and inferring disease relevance? Select all correct options.
A: Detection of Eimeria DNA by NGS is sufficient evidence that the sampled birds have clinical coccidiosis and poor host resistance.
B: qPCR can help benchmark NGS findings and provide parasite-load information relevant to disease risk, but low sensitivity for low-read-coverage OTUs may prevent reliable quantification of those minority detections.
C: Minority Eimeria OTUs detected by 18S rDNA NGS but not consistently confirmed by qPCR could represent higher analytical sensitivity, DNA from parasites replicating elsewhere in the gut and passing through the caeca, residual non-replicating material, or false-positive detections.
D: Further validation of Eimeria NGS assays would be strengthened by including control samples such as defined mixtures of purified Eimeria genomic DNA.
Contextual materials: Two quantitative PCR protocols were applied to subsets of the samples defined by 18S rDNA NGS to provide biological positive control. In all but one example the identity of the dominant Eimeria species was validated by at least one of the qPCR assays. Comparison of results for the minority OTUs suggested significantly greater sensitivity for the 18S rDNA NGS, likely permitting detection of genomic DNA originating from Eimeria species replicating higher up the gastrointestinal tract and transiting through the caeca. As an alternative, it is possible that even residual non-replicating parasite material ingested from the environment might have been detected. Such apparent variation in sensitivity remains a pertinent question with a high false-positive rate an alternative explanation. Future development of NGS approaches for use with Eimeria would benefit from the inclusion of additional control samples such as defined mixtures of pure eimerian genomic DNA. Knowledge defining Eimeria species occurrence can be of value to flock productivity and welfare, but beyond validation of the NGS protocol quantitative abundance is required to determine the risk of disease. Similarly, parasite presence/absence is not necessarily a measure of host resistance to a parasite. Levels of colonisation and replication are more relevant. Quantitative PCR can be used to benchmark NGS microbiome data and facilitate a direct assessment of parasite load, and thus risk of disease. However, the lower sensitivity of the qPCR protocols for OTUs represented by low read coverage in individual samples precluded such analysis here. It is important to note that the detection of Eimeria, or eimerian DNA, does not inevitably associate with clinical disease, although it should encourage improved anticoccidial control through husbandry, chemoprophylaxis and/or vaccination.

question: A multivariate logistic regression model for tuberculosis occurrence in livestock used cattle, winter, Bejaia province, and year 2024 as reference categories. Reported adjusted associations included: sheep OR = 0.03 (95% CI <0.01–0.06, p < 0.001), goats OR = 0.02 (95% CI <0.01–0.05, p < 0.001), autumn OR = 1.18 (95% CI 0.92–1.50, p = 0.058), summer OR = 0.82 (95% CI 0.63–1.06, p = 0.126), spring OR = 0.95 (p > 0.05), Jijel province OR = 0.68 (p = 0.009), rainfall OR = 1.06 per 10 mm (p = 0.023), and temperature OR = 0.96 per 1°C (p = 0.073). Using a conventional α = 0.05, which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: Sheep and goats had markedly lower adjusted odds of tuberculosis infection than cattle, and these differences were statistically significant.
B: Jijel province had significantly lower adjusted odds than Bejaia, corresponding to an approximate 32% reduction in odds.
C: Each additional 10 mm of rainfall was associated with approximately 6% higher adjusted odds of infection, and this association was statistically significant.
D: Autumn and higher temperature were both statistically significant predictors because their odds ratios differed from 1.0.
Contextual materials: Multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to determine the strength of the association between the occurrence of tuberculosis and its risk factors (Table 3). Cattle were the most affected species and served as the reference group. The odds of infection were significantly negligible in sheep $( \mathrm { O R } = 0 . 0 3 , \mathrm { C I } 9 5 \% \cdot < 0 . 0 1 - 0 . 0 6 , p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ and goats $( \mathrm { O R } = 0 . 0 2 , \mathrm { C I } 9 5 \% \cdot < 0 . 0 1 - 0 . 0 5 , p < 0 . 0 0 1 )$ when compared to cattle. Concerning the seasonality, autumn showed a high risk of infection $( \mathrm { O R } = 1 . 1 8 , \mathrm { C I } 9 5 \% \colon 0 . 9 2 { - 1 . 5 } , p = 0 . 0 5 8 )$ , and summer showed a reduced risk of infection (OR = 0.82, CI 95%: 0.63–1.06, p = 0.126) compared to the season reference (winter). Spring was stable in terms of infection risk versus the winter season $( \mathrm { O R } = 0 . 9 5 , p > 0 . 0 5 )$ . Using 2024 as the reference, infection odds were lower in 2019 (OR = 0.71), and moderate risk in 2020 (OR = 0.89) and 2023 (OR = 0.85), indicating a rising trend towards the 2024 peak. The province of Jijel presented a significantly lower risk of tuberculosis infection than the province of Bejaia $( \mathrm { O R } = 0 . 6 8 , p = 0 . 0 0 9 )$ , which represents a risk reduction of 32%. Increased rainfall was associated with higher infection odds (OR = 1.06 per 10 mm, p = 0.023), while higher temperatures reduced infection risk $( \mathrm { O R } = 0 . 9 6 \mathrm { p e r } 1 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } , p = 0 . 0 7 3 )$ . Relative humidity showed a non-significant trend.

question: In a molecular epidemiology study of equine Theileria haneyi, investigators amplify full-length 18S rRNA from T. haneyi-positive horses but the animals are also co-infected with T. equi, and the PCR primers can amplify both organisms. Which interpretations are scientifically appropriate? Select all correct options.
A: Poor-quality or mixed 18S amplicon data from co-infected horses can prevent reliable phylogenetic tree construction, even when a full-length 18S target was amplified.
B: The availability of a complete genome for one T. haneyi strain is sufficient to assume that alternative loci are already well defined for global strain comparison.
C: If previous Spanish equine piroplasm phylogenies detected only clades A, D, and E, newly detected Spanish T. haneyi infections can be assigned away from clade C without further sequence analysis.
D: EMA genes such as EMA10, EMA12, or EMA13 may be useful candidate markers for T. haneyi, but their diagnostic or phylogenetic value requires validation because they may not be conserved across all strains.
Contextual materials: Another limitation of our study was the absence of phylogenetic tree analysis to further compare with those previously described T. haneyi strain worldwide. Although the full length 18S was amplified and sequenced in the three T. haneyi positive Spanish horses, the amplicons had a poor quality for performing phylogenetic analysis, since the three horses were also co-infected with T. equi, which also generated amplicons due to primer cross-reactivity in the PCR reaction. However, despite full genome sequence has been recently reported for Eagle Pass T. haneyi strain, given the novelty of this species, other loci sequences remain poorly defined. In addition, although other EMA genes (e.g., EMA10, EMA12, EMA13) could be unique for T. haneyi, it might not be conservative among some T. haneyi strains (e.g., U.S. Eagle Pass, Spain, China, and other countries). Thus, additional studies are necessary to evaluate whether T. haneyi strains expressing diferent EMA genes are circulating in equids in Spain, and whether the T. haneyi strain detected in Spain could be allocated within clade C (T. haneyi-like group). Although a previous phylogenetical analysis in Spain identified only clades A, D, and E.

question: An exploratory pharmacokinetic study in dogs given oral sorafenib found that peak plasma concentrations occurred between 2 and 12 hours after dosing, mean Cmax after a 3 mg/kg dose was approximately 54.9 ng/mL, systemic exposure varied substantially among dogs, and mean serum concentrations declined by more than 70% from peak by 24 hours. Human data report similarly variable sorafenib concentrations without clear dose dependency, little effect of food on pharmacokinetics, and no clear relationship between exposure variability and adverse-event severity. Which interpretations are justified? Select all correct options.
A: The observed Tmax range is compatible with oral gastrointestinal absorption and indicates that peak sampling limited to only the first hour after dosing could miss Cmax in some dogs.
B: A mean Cmax of approximately 54.9 ng/mL after 3 mg/kg supports the possibility that this dose can reach concentrations within the range expected to inhibit biochemical targets.
C: The high interpatient variability establishes dose-proportional pharmacokinetics and confirms that dogs with higher exposure will predictably develop more severe adverse events.
D: The marked decline by 24 hours supports evaluating twice-daily dosing to maintain trough concentrations, while also monitoring for delayed toxicity from possible accumulation.
Contextual materials: Sorafenib drug concentrations measured in this exploratory study identified several pharmacokinetic features consistent with those previously reported in human Phase I clinical trials, including considerable interpatient PK variability and peak sorafenib concentrations occurring between 1 and 12 h. Sorafenib is a small lipophilic molecule with low-solubility and high permeability and following oral administration, it is rapidly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract. In our study population, the time to peak drug concentrations (Tmax) were reached between 2- and 12-h following drug administration. Importantly, the average Cmax for dogs receiving oral sorafenib was established at 54.9 ng/mL (or 118.2 nM) in the study population which supports the notion that sorafenib doses of 3 mg/kg are adequate to achieve drug exposures within the range of putative biochemical target inhibition. High interpatient variability in systemic exposure was observed in dogs receiving oral sorafenib. This is concordant with reported findings from four Phase I monotherapy trials in human patients treated with sorafenib demonstrating considerable interpatient plasma concentration variability of sorafenib with no clear dose dependency. In addition, food intake has been reported to have no appreciable impact on sorafenib PK or metabolism. Interestingly, the observed interpatient PK variability does not appear to be related to the incidence or severity of drug-related AEs in humans receiving sorafenib. The small population size and low incidence of AEs in our canine study population preclude definitive statements regarding the severity of sorafenibinduced AEs and cumulative dose and sorafenib exposure level. Lastly, mean serum sorafenib levels declined by over 70% relative to peak concentrations by 24 h in all dogs. This decline in serum drug levels is consistent with the reported half-life of sorafenib (20 to 36 h) and suggests the need for a twice daily dosing schedule in dogs to achieve putative trough target concentration. Given the presumed long half-life of sorafenib in dogs, future tolerability studies in tumor-bearing dogs administered sorafenib on a twice daily dosing schedule are necessary to assess the potential for delayed adverse event development secondary to drug accumulation.

question: In a biogeographic assessment of bat-associated argasid soft ticks, investigators compared tick occurrence records with the known ranges of their primary bat hosts. Which statements are valid interpretations of such host–parasite distribution data? Select all correct options.
A: Primary-host use may overlap substantially among soft tick species; for example, one bat species can serve as the primary host for three different tick species, while several other bat species regularly harbor two argasid species.
B: The predominant pattern is that soft tick distributions are largely independent of primary bat host ranges, indicating that host geography is generally a poor predictor of tick occurrence.
C: If Secretargas transgariepinus is recorded in northeastern Africa on Rhinopoma and Taphozous bats where its Western Palearctic primary hosts are absent, this supports the possibility of additional African primary hosts.
D: Northern records of S. transgariepinus larvae from actively migrating Pipistrellus bats could represent accidental overshooting during migration rather than established local tick populations.
Contextual materials: There is a considerable overlap between primary hosts among the diferent soft tick species. One bat species (Pipistrellus kuhlii) is the primary host for three diferent tick species, while further nine bat species regularly harbor two diferent argasid species (Table 2; Figure 6). Most tick species show a distribution that considerably overlaps with the range of their primary bat host (Figures 1, 2, 4, 5), with two notable exceptions. Secretargas transgariepinus shows a reduced range in comparison to its primary hosts’ range, with several records in NE Africa, where primary hosts registered in the Western Palearctic do not occur (Figure 3). Records in this area came from bats exclusively distributed in Africa (Rhinopoma spp., Taphozous spp.), suggesting that on the African continent other primary hosts may occur. This species is well-known to regularly occur on bats performing large scale migrations like Pipistrellus spp., hence several northern records may suggest accidental overshoots of argasid larvae collected from a bat in active migration. Another notable exception is the sole record of R. salahi in the Iberian Peninsula (Figure 5), far from the main range of its sole primary host, Rousettus aegyptius.

question: Frunevetmab is used for chronic pain associated with degenerative joint disease in cats and has been evaluated after intravenous and subcutaneous administration as well as in field studies with repeated dosing. Which statements correctly describe its mechanism, pharmacokinetics, or immunogenicity? Select all correct options.
A: Population pharmacokinetic modeling poorly predicted field-study trough concentrations and indicated that trough concentrations remained far from steady state after two doses.
B: It is a felinized monoclonal antibody that binds nerve growth factor, thereby reducing pain by blocking NGF-induced receptor-mediated signaling rather than acting as a cyclooxygenase inhibitor.
C: After 3 mg/kg dosing in cats with naturally occurring osteoarthritis, intravenous administration had an approximate 10-day half-life, while subcutaneous administration showed incomplete bioavailability of about 60% and peak concentrations several days after dosing.
D: Anti-drug antibody testing indicated a very low apparent incidence of treatment-emergent immunogenicity in treated cats, with no immunogenicity-attributed safety findings and minimal observed effect on exposure or efficacy.
Contextual materials: Osteoarthritis and other degenerative joint diseases are common causes of chronic pain in cats. Frunevetmab is a felinized monoclonal antibody that binds to nerve growth factor (NGF) and provides relief from pain by blocking the receptor-mediated signaling cascade induced by NGF. Results from three studies were combined to provide an overview of frunevetmab pharmacokinetics (PK) and immunogenicity. The objective of the first study was to establish the pharmacokinetic parameters resulting from intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration of frunevetmab to the feline patient population at 3 mg/kg. Ten adult cats with naturally-occurring osteoarthritis were administered frunevetmab in a crossover design at 28 day intervals. Non-compartmental pharmacokinetic analysis of the plasma concentration-time data showed that the half-life was $1 0 . 1 \pm 1 . 9$ days after IV dosing and the SC bioavailability was $6 0 . 3 \pm 1 5 . 8 \%$ with maximum drug levels observed at 3–7 days after dosing. Plasma samples were collected at ∼28 days after dosing during two field safety and effectiveness studies of cats with degenerative joint disease. The doses ranged from 1.0 to 2.8 mg/kg; 2 or 3 doses were administered either SC/IV, SC/SC, or SC/SC/SC. The data from these studies along with the data from the laboratory pharmacokinetic study were analyzed using non-linear mixed-effects (NLME) modeling. The model closely predicted the trough concentrations from the two field studies, including the IV treatment in the pilot field study. The trough concentrations were predicted to be close to steady-state after 2 doses. A second objective was to determine the incidence and clinical relevance of frunevetmab immunogenicity. A three-tier anti-drug antibody assay (screen, confirm, titer) was developed and validated. Immunogenicity was assessed in 259 frunevetmab-treated animals enrolled in the two field studies. Only 4 of these animals (1.5%) appeared to develop immunogenicity to frunevetmab. None of the four exhibited adverse events attributed to immunogenicity and no impact on drug levels or efficacy was observed in three of the animals. In the placebo animals, 2.3% (3/131) appeared to develop treatment-emergent immunogenicity. Overall, frunevetmab administration resulted in a very low incidence of treatment-emergent immunogenicity with no safety findings and minimal effect on drug exposure and efficacy.

question: In a reproductive pathology study of sheep, uterine tryptase immunostaining is used to assess mast cells during the follicular phase of the estrous cycle. Which statements correctly interpret expected mast-cell distribution, function, and endocrine associations in mammalian uterine tissue? Select all correct options.
A: Tryptase-positive mast cells may be found in uterine connective tissue and around blood vessels of the stratum vascularis.
B: Uterine mast-cell mediators such as histamine can participate in tissue remodeling and influence ovulation, embryo implantation, and myometrial contractility.
C: Reported endocrine correlations of uterine mast cells are species dependent, including associations with estrogen in sows and rats and with progesterone in the canine uterus.
D: Uterine mast-cell number and morphology are generally fixed across the estrous or menstrual cycle and are not influenced by ovarian steroid variation.
Contextual materials: Interestingly, tryptase-positive immunostaining mast cells were recruited in the uterine connective tissue and around the blood vessels of the stratum vascularis. MCs during the follicular phase of the estrous cycle play a crucial role in secreting substances that promote tissue remodeling. Histamine is one of these important substances released from uterine mast cells, influencing ovulation, embryo implantation, and myometrium contractility leading to successful implantation and ultimately to parturition. However, spatiotemporally expression of MCs in the female reproductive tract has been reported in other studies. In the uterus, they change in number and structure depending on the hormonal level variations during the menstrual or estrous cycle. A previous study has revealed alterations in the characteristics and location of MCs in mice, rats, hamsters, cows, and guinea pigs uterine tissues during pregnancy and estrous cycle. Notably, the number and activity of MCs are correlated with estrogen concentrations in the uterine tissue of sows and rats, while they are correlated with progesterone concentrations in the canine uterus.

question: In a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic assessment of transdermal flunixin meglumine use in pre-weaned piglets, investigators treated therapeutic NSAID activity as requiring at least 80% inhibition of COX-2. Flunixin is a non-selective COX inhibitor, and COX-1 inhibition is associated with gastrointestinal adverse effects such as intestinal erosions and ulceration. Because swine-specific COX-1 and COX-2 IC50/IC80 values were not available, equine values were used for extrapolation. Monte Carlo simulations predicted that increasing the transdermal dose as high as 20 mg/kg would keep concentrations above the COX-2 IC80 target for less than 1 hour while increasing COX-1 inhibition for more than 2 hours. Which interpretations are justified? Select all correct options.
A: The extrapolation from equine COX inhibition values represents a methodological limitation because swine-specific IC50 and IC80 values were unavailable.
B: The predicted exposure profile suggests a poor therapeutic index, because COX-2 target attainment is brief while potentially toxic COX-1 inhibition is more prolonged.
C: Escalating the transdermal dose to 20 mg/kg would be expected to provide prolonged COX-2-mediated anti-inflammatory exposure suitable for sustained analgesia in these piglets.
D: The gastrointestinal safety concern is mechanistically linked to flunixin’s non-selective inhibition of COX-1 within the arachidonic acid pathway.
Contextual materials: Research on NSAIDs has shown that the ability to achieve a therapeutic efect is dependent upon the ability to achieve at least 80% inhibition (IC ) of COX-2. As a non-selective COX inhibitor, FM also inhibits COX-1, which is associated with unwanted gastrointestinal toxicities such as intestinal erosions and ulceration. The authors conducted a literature search and are not aware of research that has established swine $\mathrm { I C } _ { 5 0 }$ and $\mathrm { I C } _ { 8 0 }$ values for the COX isoforms. Although the use of values from another species is a study limitation, it is well documented that NSAIDs cause GI toxicity due to their action on the arachidonic acid pathway; therefore, data from equine research was used in this study to extrapolate swine $\mathrm { I C } _ { 5 0 }$ and $\mathrm { I C } _ { 8 0 }$ to determine anti-COX activity. A core objective of this study was to estimate a therapeutic and safe dose for TD FM in piglets. Our Monte Carlo simulations show that increasing the FM TD dose up to 20 mg/kg provides FM concentrations above the $\mathrm { I C } _ { 8 0 }$ target for COX-2 for <1 h. Incidentally, this very high dose would cause increased COX-1 inhibition for ${ > } 2 \mathrm { h }$ . Overall, these results suggest that this increased formulation of TD FM is unable to provide systemic antiinflammatory concentration that are consistent with pain relief in pre-wean piglets.

question: In a postoperative analgesia trial in cats undergoing ovariohysterectomy, groups received either low-dose dipyrone combined with tramadol, tramadol alone, or dipyrone alone. During 5 days of follow-up, rescue analgesia was required in 1 cat in the combination group, compared with 4 cats receiving tramadol alone and 5 cats receiving dipyrone alone. Prior feline data showed that dipyrone 25 mg/kg once daily was associated with about 40% rescue analgesia, whereas 12.5 mg/kg administered more frequently was associated with about 20%; tramadol 2 mg/kg alone has been associated with about 50% rescue analgesia. Dipyrone and tramadol are rapidly metabolized hepatically to active compounds, 4-aminoantipyrine and O-desmethyltramadol, respectively. Which interpretations are best supported? Select all correct options.
A: The prior dipyrone findings indicate that 25 mg/kg once daily is more effective than lower, more frequent dosing in reducing rescue analgesia in cats.
B: The low rescue-analgesia requirement with the combination, despite the low tramadol dose, is consistent with a possible synergistic analgesic interaction.
C: Pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interactions between the active metabolites remain biologically plausible because both metabolites can contribute to analgesic mechanisms.
D: The lack of unexpected adverse effects proves that no clinically relevant interaction can occur between dipyrone and tramadol metabolites.
Contextual materials: In this study, the lower dose of dipyrone combined with tramadol provided efective analgesia, with only one cat requiring rescue at a single time point during the 5-day follow-up. In contrast, the groups receiving tramadol or dipyrone alone had 4 and 5 animals needing rescue analgesia, respectively. These findings agree with previous studies reporting 30–40% rescue rates when dipyrone at 25 mg/kg was used alone for neutering female cats or dogs. In a previous study by our group in cats, we verified that with the 25 mg/kg dose daily, the percentage of cats needing rescue medication doubled compared to those receiving 12.5 mg/kg every 12.5 h, being 40 and 20%, respectively. Considering the low tramadol dose (2 mg/kg), the synergistic efect of the combination is implied. Brondani et al. reported a 50% need for rescue medication with this dose in cats submitted to OVH, a result very similar to our prior findings. Metamizole and tramadol undergo rapid hepatic metabolism to their active compounds, 4-aminoantipyrine and O-desmethyltramadol (M1), respectively. Potential pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interactions between these metabolites cannot be excluded, particularly considering that both contribute to central and peripheral analgesic mechanisms. Experimental evidence has previously suggested a synergistic analgesic interaction between tramadol and metamizole in dogs. In the present study, however, no additive or unexpected adverse efects were observed, supporting the clinical tolerability of this combination in cats.

question: A canine pharmacokinetic study evaluated oral sapanisertib given every other day, either alone or with trametinib. Sapanisertib was rapidly absorbed, with an average Tmax of approximately 2 hours, and showed no meaningful accumulation during repeated every-other-day dosing. In the combination group, sapanisertib Cmax and AUC were lower than with sapanisertib alone, and apparent clearance was higher with a greater apparent volume of distribution. Sapanisertib had little apparent effect on trametinib pharmacokinetics. Trametinib accumulated during repeat dosing and is known to induce CYP3A4 in other species. Which interpretations are most pharmacokinetically appropriate? Select all correct options.
A: The absence of sapanisertib accumulation during every-other-day dosing indicates saturable clearance and predicts progressively increasing exposure with continued dosing.
B: The lower sapanisertib exposure during trametinib coadministration is consistent with induction of a CYP3A-family metabolic pathway increasing sapanisertib clearance.
C: Because sapanisertib did not substantially alter trametinib pharmacokinetics, a reciprocal absence of interaction should be assumed, excluding any trametinib effect on sapanisertib exposure.
D: Accumulation of trametinib during repeat dosing could plausibly intensify microsomal enzyme induction and contribute to further reduction of sapanisertib exposure at later sampling times.
Contextual materials: Sapanisertib was rapidly absorbed by dogs (Tmax 2 h on average) and did not display accumulation with repeated QOD dosing. The pharmacokinetic profile findings were similar to single-agent human studies. While the presence of sapanisertib lacked substantial efect on trametinib PK when given in combination, the reverse proved otherwise. On day 1, both sapanisertib $\mathrm { C _ { M A X } }$ and AUC (AUC ) were significantly less in the combination arm vs. sapanisertib alone, a finding that was foreshadowed in a mouse model. In combination with trametinib, sapanisertib clearance in these Group 3 dogs was faster and distribution volume greater (lower exposure) compared to dogs in Group 2 treated with sapanisertib alone, outcomes that are consistent with a compensatory action for the lower AUC. Trametinib is a known inducer of cytochrome P450 CYP3A4. Thus, induction of cytochrome P450 is a likely mechanism behind the faster clearance and lower exposure $( \mathrm { C _ { M A X } }$ and AUC) of sapanisertib during combination treatment, relative to sapanisertib alone. This is at least consistent as well with the additional accumulation of trametinib during repeat dosing and that being plausibly accompanied by further cytochrome P450 microsomal induction, which could therefore consequently be reflected in the observed continued sapanisertib diminution when combined with trametinib at the later time point. Unfortunately, published evidence to confirm the specific CYP isoform was not uncovered, but based on this dog study, CYP3A family induction appears to be a candidate metabolic mechanism.

question: In evaluating intestinal lesions of paratuberculosis in naturally infected goats, which statements correctly distinguish typical caprine findings and relevant histologic scoring considerations? Select all correct options.
A: Failure to detect gross intestinal lesions at necropsy does not rule out caprine paratuberculosis, whereas cattle more commonly show diffusely thickened, corrugated intestinal mucosal folds.
B: Intestinal mucosal ulceration is a required and consistent gross lesion in both clinical and subclinical caprine paratuberculosis.
C: A histologic scoring approach based only on hematoxylin-eosin lesions should not be altered by the acid-fast bacillus burden seen with Ziehl-Neelsen staining.
D: Separately assessing lamina propria and Peyer’s patches can be justified because lesions may differ between these sites, and focal lesions are generally uncommon in goats.
Contextual materials: Gross PTB lesions affecting the intestines were detected in only 7/39 of the cases. The absence of macroscopic lesions has been previously described as a common finding in goat PTB in contrast with bovine PTB, where classic diffusely thickened corrugated intestinal mucosa folds are commonly observed. Some authors describe ulceration of the intestinal mucosa in both clinical and subclinical cases, but such findings were not observed in the animals studied. Histological evaluation of the intestine was carried out following the score proposed per Krüger et al. This score is based on histological lesions observed only with hematoxylin-eosin stain and is not influenced by AFB load detected with ZN as the one proposed by Corpa et al., for naturally infected goats. Modifications were introduced to separately evaluate the LP and the PP based on differences described in previous studies regarding the difference between the type of lesions described in those two locations. Regarding the histological lesions described, our result agrees with previous studies which suggest that goats have limited ability to control mycobacterial infections and focal lesions are rarely seen.

question: A veterinary pathologist investigates episodic mortality and population declines in invasive blue crabs (Callinectes sapidus) from several Greek coastal fishing sites. Both lethargic and apparently healthy crabs are sampled; hemolymph appearance, histopathology of heart, gills, and hepatopancreas, and molecular assays for parasites are evaluated. Which statements correctly interpret findings consistent with Hematodinium perezi-associated disease in this scenario? Select all correct options.
A: A diagnosis of H. perezi disease would be supported only by superficial shell lesions, because this dinoflagellate does not involve internal organs.
B: Lethargy accompanied by a milky discoloration of the hemolymph is compatible with early parasitic infestation by H. perezi.
C: Detection of H. perezi by histopathology and molecular methods in heart, gills, and hepatopancreas, with hemocyte-associated tissue disruption, supports a role in crab mortality.
D: Finding Epistylis sp. on the gills is best interpreted as an epibiotic peritrich ciliate infection rather than proof that it is the primary systemic cause of mortality.
Contextual materials: Abstract: Bioinvasions constitute both a direct and an indirect threat to ecosystems. Direct threats include pressures on local trophic chains, while indirect threats might take the form of an invasion of a microorganism alongside its host. The marine dinoflagellate Hematodinium perezi, parasitizing blue crabs (Callinectes sapidus), has a worldwide distribution alongside its host. In Greece, fluctuations in the blue crab population are attributed to overexploitation and the effects of climate change. The hypothesis of the present study was that blue crab population reductions cannot only be due to these factors, and that particular pathogens may also be responsible for the fluctuations. To investigate this hypothesis, both lethargic and healthy blue crab specimens were collected from three different fishing sites in order to assess the health status of this important species. Together with the lethargic responses, the hemolymph of the infested crabs presented a milky hue, indicating the first signs of parasitic infestation with H. perezi. The histopathological results and molecular identification demonstrated the effect of the presence of H. perezi in the internal organs and their important role in the mortality of blue crabs. Specifically, H. perezi, in three different tissues examined (heart, gills, hepatopancreas), affected the hemocytes of the species, resulting in alterations in tissue structure. Apart from this dinoflagellate parasite, the epibiotic peritrich ciliate Epistylis sp. was also identified, infecting the gills. This study represents the first detection of H. perezi in the eastern Mediterranean, demonstrating that this is the main causative agent of blue crab mortality on Greek coastlines.

question: A 10-year-old neutered male dog presents with progressive dysuria, pelvic discomfort, and an enlarged irregular prostate. Prostatic abscess and prostatic carcinoma are both considered, but the owner has financial constraints. Which statements correctly describe diagnostic and biologic considerations for suspected canine prostatic adenocarcinoma? Select all correct options.
A: Histopathologic examination of invasively obtained prostatic tissue is the most accurate basis for confirming carcinoma when imaging and clinical signs are equivocal.
B: Computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging may be prioritized diagnostically, and CT is particularly valuable when metastatic disease is suspected.
C: Canine prostatic adenocarcinoma is often aggressive and may metastasize to pelvic or lumbar lymph nodes as well as distant sites such as bone or brain.
D: Prostatic adenocarcinoma in dogs is typically androgen-dependent, so prior castration makes this diagnosis unlikely.
Contextual materials: It is dificult to distinguish between prostate abscess and prostate cancer without biopsy. CT examination and magnetic resonance imaging are a priority, but the high cost of the examination is unacceptable to many owners, thus limiting practical application. CT examination is of great application value when metastatic lesions are suspected. At present, invasive sampling for pathological tissue section examination is the most accurate basis for cancer diagnosis. In prostate cancer, some acinar structures can be observed in pathological tissue sections, while urothelial cells show tail shapes and sporadic cytoplasmic vacuoles with bright pink material; however, these features are not present in all cases. The tissue examined in this case showed epithelial cancer cell infiltration. Based on the clinical information and the location of the lesion, adenocarcinoma of the prostate is the most consistent diagnosis. Prostatic adenocarcinoma is not dependent on androgen (the dog has been castrated 6years ago), and about 70–80% of cases will have aggressive move quickly, often can be transferred to the pelvis and lumbar lymph nodes, but are visible extensive transferred to the various organs, including bone (lumbar) and brain. Such lesions usually have a high mortality rate and short survival time, and are often associated with not being diagnosed until the advanced stage of the disease.

question: A feline pharmacokinetic study of orally administered gabapentin reports a Tmax of 1.83 hours, an absolute bioavailability of 78.71%, and a half-life of 5.6 hours. The investigators note that human and canine gabapentin bioavailability values are approximately 74.1% and 80%, respectively, whereas an equine value is approximately 16.2%. They also state that bioavailability was calculated using data from different individual animals. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: The reported 78.71% value indicates high oral bioavailability because absolute bioavailability represents the proportion of active drug reaching systemic circulation.
B: The feline bioavailability estimate is broadly comparable to reported human and canine values but substantially higher than the reported equine value.
C: Calculating bioavailability between different individuals would be expected to eliminate interanimal pharmacokinetic variability from the estimate.
D: Differences between the observed feline half-life and prior feline reports could plausibly reflect variation in study design, breed, age, or gabapentin formulation.
Contextual materials: The bioavailability of a drug is defined as the proportion of the active ingredient that reaches systemic circulation. An absolute bioavailability of greater than 50% is generally considered to indicate high oral bioavailability. The bioavailability was calculated between different individuals, which may have introduced variability. We compared our pharmacokinetic findings with prior feline studies. Our results showed that the Tmax and bioavailability were 1.83 h and 78.71%, which are consistent with previous feline studies. In addition, the bioavailability of $\mathrm { G B P }$ in humans (74.1%) and dogs (80%) is comparable to what we reported, but significantly higher than that in horses (16.2%). Furthermore, the half-life we observed was 5.6 h, which is different to that in previous reports. These differences may be due to factors such as variations in study design, cat breeds, ages or the specific formulations of GBP used.

question: In a dairy-cow lameness study evaluating parity-related risk for claw horn disruption lesions around calving, lesion categories included sole hemorrhage (SH), sole ulcer (SU), and white line disease (WLD). Which statements correctly interpret the reported parity associations and proposed mechanisms? Select all correct options.
A: Primiparous cows are expected to develop SU or WLD rather than SH because previous chronic claw horn lesions and exostosis are already well established by first calving.
B: Second-parity cows would be expected to have the highest SU incidence because their digital cushion is less developed than in primiparous cows and they have the greatest cumulative calving-associated chronic inflammation.
C: Primiparous cows may have higher odds of SH but lower odds of WLD than multiparous cows, potentially because a developing digital cushion, lower body forces through the foot, and minimal exostosis favor a milder lesion phenotype.
D: Cows in third or greater parity may have higher odds of SU than second-parity cows, while not necessarily having significantly higher SU incidence than primiparous cows, suggesting a non-linear parity relationship with SU risk.
Contextual materials: SST compared to multiparous cows, which is supported by the existing literature. Our results have shown that primiparous animals had higher odds of developing SH compared to multiparous animals, but had lower odds of developing WLD. This finding was again supported by previous findings. One hypothesis is that the composition of the developing digital cushion has a somewhat protective function, together with the reduced forces going through the foot of comparatively lighter animals around calving when the insult is expected to have occurred, especially in primiparous animals where calving is expected to be more challenging as they are added to the herd and undergo parturition for the first time. Additionally, given these are naïve animals which are unlikely to have experienced CHDL’s, exostosis is unlikely to significantly afect the development of these lesions. Therefore, SH occurs rather than a SU or WLD, given SH is thought to be a precursor or result from a milder insult. Animals in their third or greater than third parity were at higher odds of developing SU comparing to animals in their second parity. The efect of exostosis, digital cushion composition, increased force through feet and the stress of calving could increase the risk of animals in their third or greater than third parity forming SU and WLD over SH. However, animals in their third or greater than third parity did not have a significantly higher SU incidence than primiparous animals and this suggests a “non-linear” association between parity and incidence of SU, with second parity animals having the lowest incidence. This contradicts previous findings that suggested that SU incidence is lower in primiparous animals. The reason behind this finding is unclear; a possible explanation is that animals in their second parity may benefit from a more developed DC (comparing to primiparous animals) but are yet to experience the increased risk associated with multiple calvings and chronic inflammation that may be more evident in animals in their third or greater than third parity.

question: A randomized clinical mastitis trial in dairy cows used bacteriological cure as the primary outcome. The antibiotic reference group had a cure risk of 48.1%, and the NSAID-only group had a cure risk of 45.6%. A conventional significance test found no statistically significant difference between groups. The prespecified non-inferiority margin was 15%, but the confidence interval for the treatment contrast slightly crossed the non-inferiority boundary. The trial enrolled only cows with long-lasting udder disease, a subgroup expected to have a relatively low probability of bacteriological cure. Which interpretations are correct? Select all correct options.
A: The absence of a statistically significant difference does not by itself establish non-inferiority when the confidence interval crosses the prespecified margin.
B: Because the NSAID group’s cure risk was only slightly lower than the antibiotic group’s, NSAID therapy must be considered definitively non-inferior regardless of the confidence interval.
C: If the point estimate remained similar, a larger sample size could narrow the confidence interval and potentially permit a conclusive non-inferiority finding.
D: A low overall bacteriological cure risk in this selected population is compatible with the enrollment of cows with long-lasting udder disease rather than all mastitis cases occurring in a herd.
Contextual materials: The primary outcome in this trial was BC. Although BC risk of the reference group with antibiotic treatment was numerically higher with 48.1% compared to the NSAID group with 45.6%, no significant diferences were confirmed by statistical analysis. As the CI spans the non-inferiority margin (–1), non-inferiority was inconclusive but very close to non-inferior for NSAID treatment in comparison to the solely antibiotic treatment (Figure 1). An inconclusive result could possibly occur due to a wide range of the CI. However, the confidence interval only slightly exceeded delta. With a larger number of cases, the non-inferiority could possibly be confirmed, as the span of the CI would become smaller. The non-inferiority margin of 15% was chosen according to previous CM trials. Sample size was calculated to give the study suficient power and to show a diference between test and reference therapy if there was a real diference of at least 15% according to Schukken et al. The NSAID treatment in our study showed a numerically almost identical BC risk and no significant diferences to the reference treatment; non-inferiority was inconclusive due to the lack of power. The overall BC risk was low in this study with 44.4%, as was the BC risk for CM cases treated with antibiotics (48.1%). This study exclusively included CM cases of cows with long-lasting udder diseases. Therefore, low likelihood of BC was expected, as studies had shown before. In comparison, focusing on all occurring cases in a dairy herd, studies demonstrated BC risks of ∼70%. The high diferences in BC rates support the selection criteria used in this study to choose cows sufering from CM with a low likelihood of BC. Nevertheless, a tendency for the eficacy of antibiotic treatment against mastitis pathogens was shown.

question: A dairy herd study finds that enteric Enterococcus spp. from adult lactating cows have very high antimicrobial resistance to florfenicol and macrolides, even though these drugs are not approved for use in lactating dairy cows and herd records show no adult-cow administration. Which interpretations are epidemiologically and mechanistically plausible? Select all correct options.
A: The lack of recorded adult-cow florfenicol or macrolide treatment excludes antimicrobial exposure as a contributor and makes spontaneous de novo mutation the only plausible explanation.
B: Resistance may be promoted by co-selection if genes conferring florfenicol resistance are located on plasmids with genes conferring resistance to other antimicrobials used on the farm.
C: Use of recycled lagoon water to flush free-stall pens could indirectly expose adult cows to resistant bacteria or antimicrobial residues present in excreta or secretions.
D: Florfenicol and macrolide use in calves, such as for respiratory disease, could contribute residues or resistant organisms to the farm environment that later contact adult cows.
Contextual materials: Cow-level ES AMR incidence ranged from 1.7% for penicillin to >90% for florfenicol and macrolides (tildipirosin or tilmicosin), which showed that enteric ES had a higher rate of AMR for drugs not approved for use in lactating dairy cows despite the study herds’ treatment records showing no administrations of macrolides or florfenicol in adult cows. Other studies similarly reported AMR to florfenicol and macrolides in Enterococcus spp. isolated from dairy cows. Another study reported that the predominant AMR genes in Enterococcus spp. from dairy cattle in CA targeted macrolide drugs. The high levels of resistance for florfenicol and macrolides in enteric ES detected in our study could be attributed to the mechanism of co-selection, similar to that related to systemic administration of ceftiofur hydrochloride and its associated increase in tetracycline resistance in E. coli. Florfenicol resistance in E. coli is associated with the floR gene, which is co-located on plasmids with genes that confer resistance to other antimicrobial drugs, which may explain florfenicol resistance spread with exposure to drugs other than florfenicol. In our study herds, the common practice of flushing free-stall pens with recycled lagoon water may have played a role in exposing adult cattle to resistant bacteria or AMD residues in excreta or secretions of cows and/or calves treated with AMD. Florfenicol and macrolides are commonly used to treat respiratory diseases in calves. Hence, recycled lagoon water may have exposed adult cows to the florfenicol and macrolide residues from treated calves.

question: A pharmacokinetic study in dogs receiving phenobarbital for 4 weeks failed to show the expected autoinduction pattern: phenobarbital clearance did not increase, elimination half-life did not shorten, and clearance was actually lower at week 4 than at baseline. Prior canine studies have reported higher phenobarbital clearance with much higher escalating doses and with longer treatment durations, including increases detected 30, 60, and 90 days after initiation. Another study found that phenobarbital-induced hepatic enzyme activity could persist for weeks after drug cessation. Which interpretations are best supported? Select all correct options.
A: A 4-week treatment period may be too short in some dogs to demonstrate increased phenobarbital clearance from autoinduction.
B: Dose and duration of phenobarbital exposure are plausible contributors to whether increased clearance is detected.
C: Failure to observe increased clearance after 4 weeks proves that phenobarbital does not induce hepatic drug-metabolizing enzymes in dogs.
D: Persistent hepatic enzyme induction after phenobarbital cessation necessarily means phenobarbital clearance must increase during every 4-week treatment protocol.
Contextual materials: Despite reports of autoinduction associated with phenobarbital induction of cytochrome 450 metabolism, we were not able to demonstrate an expected increased clearance or shortened elimination half-life of phenobarbital over the 4-week treatment period. Indeed, clearance was decreased at 4-weeks compared to baseline. It has been previously demonstrated that clearance was higher in dogs receiving a higher phenobarbital dose (escalating doses starting at \~1.2 mg/kg/d and ending at 32 mg/kg/d), and in dogs treated with phenobarbital over a longer period of time. In the latter study, a significantly higher clearance was found 30, 60, and 90 days from initial phenobarbital therapy when compared to the single dose. Furthermore, in a study investigating the lasting efects of liver enzyme induction from a 10 mg/kg/d dose of phenobarbital after a 34 day administration, activity remained enhanced for 4 weeks after cessation of phenobarbital administration in dogs administered antipyrine. In this study, initial clearance of 6.2 ± 1.5 mL/kg/h was not statistically diferent (p = 0.8) from that at the end of the study at 6.3 ± 1.3 mL/kg/h It is possible that dogs in this study were not treated with phenobarbital long enough to demonstrate an increase in clearance or there may be individual variation in autoinduction.

question: In cattle with buffalo fly-associated cutaneous lesions, diagnostic evaluation identifies variable involvement of Stephanofilaria nematodes and bacteria, while a substantial proportion of lesions lack evidence of either agent. Which interpretations of lesion pathogenesis and morphology are most appropriate? Select all correct options.
A: The absence of both detectable nematodes and bacteria in many lesions suggests that neither agent is strictly required for lesion initiation, and that fly feeding trauma or hypersensitivity may contribute.
B: Stephanofilaria-associated lesions would be expected to show relatively greater dermal injury and may be linked to dry, crusted lesion morphology.
